note: 每周一篇英语阅读（每个年级 52 篇）：原创，或改写公共领域作品。内容由模型写成，需校对。

1.text: I have a cat. Her name is Mimi. She is small and white. She likes milk. She likes fish too. Mimi is my best friend. I love my cat.

q.q: What is the cat's name?
What colour is Mimi?
What does Mimi like to drink?

1.text: Look at the sky! I see a rainbow. It is red, yellow and green. It is blue and purple too. The rainbow is big. It is so pretty. I like it.

q.q: Where is the rainbow?
Which colour is in the rainbow?
Is the rainbow big or small?

1.text: This is my family. This is my mum. This is my dad. This is my sister. She is five. I am seven. We are happy. I love my family.

q.q: How old is the sister?
How old is the child?
How is the family?

1.text: This is my school bag. It is blue. I have a pen in it. I have a ruler and a book. I have a red pencil too. I like my bag.

q.q: What colour is the bag?
What is in the bag?
What colour is the pencil?

1.text: I like fruit. I like apples. I like bananas. Bananas are yellow. Apples are red. My mum has an orange. She gives me one. Yum! I eat it.

q.q: What colour are bananas?
What does mum have?
What colour are apples?

1.text: Look at that dog. It is big and brown. Its name is Max. Max can run fast. He can jump too. He likes a ball. Max is my friend's dog.

q.q: What colour is Max?
What does Max like?
Is Max small?

1.text: We go to the zoo. I see a tall giraffe. I see a big elephant. I see a monkey. The monkey eats a banana. It is funny. I like the zoo.

q.q: Where do they go?
What does the monkey eat?
Which animal is tall?

1.text: One, two, three! I have three red apples. Four, five, six! I see six small birds. Seven, eight, nine, ten! I count ten stars. I can count to ten.

q.q: How many red apples?
How many small birds?
What can I count to?

1.text: This is my teacher. Her name is Miss Lin. She is kind. She has a red bag. She says, "Good morning, class!" We say, "Good morning, Miss Lin!" I like my teacher.

q.q: What is the teacher's name?
What colour is her bag?
What does the class say?

1.text: It is Friday. We have pizza for lunch. The pizza is hot. It has cheese on it. I eat two pieces. My friend eats three. We are full. Pizza is great!

q.q: What day is it?
How many pieces do I eat?
What is on the pizza?

1.text: A little duck is on the water. It is yellow. It says, "Quack, quack!" Its mum is near. The duck swims to its mum. They swim together. They are happy.

q.q: What colour is the duck?
What does the duck say?
Who is near the duck?

1.text: This is my bedroom. I have a small bed. It is green. I have a desk and a chair. I have a lamp on the desk. I read a book in bed. Good night!

q.q: What colour is the bed?
What is on the desk?
What do I read in bed?

1.text: The sun is in the sky. It is big and yellow. It is hot. I like the sun. I play in the park. I wear a hat. I drink some water. It is a good day.

q.q: What colour is the sun?
Where do I play?
What do I wear?

1.text: A rabbit is hungry. It sees a carrot. It eats the carrot. It sees a lettuce. It eats the lettuce. Now the rabbit is full. It goes to sleep.

q.q: What does the rabbit eat first?
How is the rabbit at first?
What does it do at the end?

1.text: I can swim. My dad is at the pool with me. He says, "Kick your legs!" I kick my legs. I move my arms. I can do it! Dad says, "Well done!"

q.q: Who is with me at the pool?
What do I kick?
What does Dad say?

1.text: It is a rainy day. I have a yellow umbrella. I wear red boots. I jump in a puddle. Splash! My boots are wet. I go home. Mum gives me a warm drink.

q.q: What colour is the umbrella?
What colour are the boots?
Who gives me a warm drink?

1.text: Today is my birthday. I am eight. I have a big cake. It has eight candles. My friends sing a song. I blow out the candles. I am very happy.

q.q: How old am I?
How many candles are there?
What do my friends do?

1.text: This is a farm. I see a cow. The cow says, "Moo!" I see a pig. The pig is pink. I see three white sheep. They eat grass. I like the farm animals.

q.q: What does the cow say?
What colour is the pig?
How many sheep are there?

1.text: I have two hands. I have two feet. I have two eyes and two ears. I have one nose and one mouth. I clap my hands. I stamp my feet. It is fun!

q.q: How many eyes do I have?
How many noses do I have?
What do I clap?

1.text: I have many toys. I have a red car. I have a doll and a teddy bear. The bear is brown and soft. I like my bear best. I sleep with it every night.

q.q: What colour is the car?
What toy do I like best?
When do I sleep with the bear?

1.text: It is night. The moon is round and bright. I see many stars in the sky. They are small. They shine. I look out of my window. Then I go to bed.

q.q: When is it?
What shape is the moon?
Where do I look?

1.text: Sam sees a green frog. The frog is by the pond. It jumps into the water. Splash! Sam laughs. The frog comes back. It sits on a big leaf. Sam says, "Hello, frog!"

q.q: What colour is the frog?
Where does the frog jump?
What does Sam do?

1.text: I get up at seven. I wash my face. Then I eat breakfast. I have an egg and some bread. I drink a glass of milk. Then I go to school with my mum.

q.q: When do I get up?
What do I drink?
Who goes to school with me?

1.text: A little red hen finds some seeds. She asks, "Who can help me?" The dog says, "No." The cat says, "No." The hen plants the seeds by herself. Later she has fresh bread.
1.src: adapted from the folk tale The Little Red Hen (traditional, public domain)

q.q: What does the hen find?
Who says no?
What does the hen have later?

1.text: My grandma has a garden. It has red roses and yellow flowers. A bee flies by. It goes from flower to flower. I smell a rose. It smells so sweet. I love the garden.

q.q: Whose garden is it?
What flies by?
How does the rose smell?

1.text: I draw a circle. It is round. I draw a square. It has four sides. I draw a triangle. It has three sides. I colour them red, blue and green. I like shapes.

q.q: How many sides has the square?
How many sides has the triangle?
Which shape is round?

1.text: It is winter. It is cold. There is snow on the ground. We make a snowman. It has a big round body. It has a carrot nose. It wears a red scarf. We love our snowman.

q.q: What is the nose made of?
What colour is the scarf?
What is on the ground?

1.text: It is Spring Festival. My family is at home. We eat dumplings. We wear new red clothes. Grandpa gives me a red envelope. I say, "Happy New Year!" We watch fireworks at night. They are so bright!

q.q: What do we eat?
Who gives me a red envelope?
When do we watch fireworks?

1.text: A tiger sleeps under a tree. A little mouse runs over him. The tiger wakes up. He is angry. The mouse says, "Please, let me go!" The tiger smiles and lets the mouse go. The mouse is very happy.
1.src: adapted from Aesop's fable The Lion and the Mouse (public domain), changed to a tiger

q.q: Where does the tiger sleep?
How is the tiger when he wakes up?
What does the tiger do at the end?

1.text: I have two pet fish. One is gold and one is orange. They live in a glass bowl. Every day I give them food. They swim round and round. I watch them for a long time. They make me calm.

q.q: How many pet fish do I have?
Where do the fish live?
What do I give them every day?

1.text: It is windy today. Dad and I go to the park. We have a big red kite. I run fast and Dad holds the string. The kite goes up, up, up! It looks like a bird in the sky.

q.q: How is the weather?
What colour is the kite?
Who holds the string?

1.text: I see a fire truck. It is red and very loud. It goes fast down the street. The firefighters wear yellow hats. They have a long hose. They help people. I want to be a firefighter.

q.q: What colour is the fire truck?
What do the firefighters wear?
What do I want to be?

1.text: Brush your teeth every morning and every night. Use a little toothpaste. Brush for two minutes. Brush the front and the back. Do not eat too many sweets. Then your teeth stay white and strong.

q.q: When do we brush our teeth?
How long do we brush?
What should we not eat too many of?

1.text: Every morning I take the bus to school. The bus is yellow. Many children are on it. I sit by the window with my friend Tom. We look at the cars and trees. Then the bus stops at our school.

q.q: What colour is the bus?
Who sits with me?
Where does the bus stop?

1.text: On Sunday we go on a picnic. Mum puts a blanket on the grass. We eat sandwiches and grapes. My little brother drinks juice. An ant walks on the blanket. We laugh. It is a lovely day with my family.

q.q: When do we go on a picnic?
What does my brother drink?
What walks on the blanket?

1.text: In autumn there is a festival for the moon. The moon is big and round. My family sits outside. We eat sweet mooncakes. Grandma tells us a story about a lady on the moon. I look up and smile.

q.q: What do we eat?
Who tells the story?
Where does my family sit?

1.text: After school I play football with my friends. I am quick. I kick the ball to Ben. Ben kicks it into the goal! We shout, "Goal!" Our team wins. We are tired but happy. We drink water and go home.

q.q: Who plays football with me?
Who kicks the ball into the goal?
How are we at the end?

1.text: The panda is black and white. It lives in China. It likes to eat bamboo all day. It has big round ears. It is slow and soft. A baby panda is very small. Many people love pandas.

q.q: What colour is a panda?
What does the panda eat?
Where does the panda live?

1.text: Mum and I go to the supermarket. We have a long list. We buy milk, eggs and rice. I push the trolley. I see my favourite biscuits. Mum says yes. At the end we pay and go home.

q.q: Where do we go?
Who pushes the trolley?
What do I see?

1.text: A thirsty crow finds a jar. There is a little water at the bottom. The crow cannot reach it. He drops small stones into the jar. The water goes up. At last the crow can drink. He is clever.
1.src: adapted from Aesop's fable The Crow and the Pitcher (public domain)

q.q: What does the crow find?
What does the crow drop in the jar?
How is the crow?

1.text: Our classroom is bright and clean. There are twenty desks and many chairs. A big map is on the wall. There is a clock too. Our teacher writes on the blackboard. I sit near the door. I like my classroom.

q.q: How many desks are there?
What is on the wall?
Where do I sit?

1.text: Summer is very hot. The sun shines all day. We wear shorts and T-shirts. We eat cold ice cream. My sister and I swim in the sea. We build a big sandcastle. The waves come and wash it away.

q.q: What do we eat in summer?
Where do we swim?
What do we build?

1.text: Today I make a fruit salad with Dad. We cut a banana, an apple and some grapes. We put them in a big bowl. Then we add a little orange juice. It is sweet and cold. My family loves it.

q.q: Who makes the salad with me?
What do we add at the end?
How does the salad taste?

1.text: People in China tell a story about a white rabbit on the moon. The rabbit lives with a kind lady. It makes medicine with a stick and a pot. On a bright night, look up. Can you see the rabbit?

q.q: What colour is the rabbit?
What does the rabbit make?
When can you look for the rabbit?

1.text: My best friend is Anna. She is eight years old. She has long black hair and a big smile. We sit together at school. We share our pencils and snacks. When I am sad, she hugs me. I am lucky.

q.q: How old is Anna?
What do we share?
What does Anna do when I am sad?

1.text: A hare laughs at a slow tortoise. "Let us race!" says the tortoise. The hare runs fast and then takes a nap. The tortoise walks and walks and does not stop. He gets to the end first. Slow and steady wins.
1.src: adapted from Aesop's fable The Tortoise and the Hare (public domain)

q.q: Who laughs at the tortoise?
What does the hare do in the race?
Who wins the race?

1.text: I have a cold today. My nose is red and I cough a lot. Mum takes me to the doctor. The doctor looks in my mouth. She says, "Drink water and rest in bed." I take my medicine and sleep. I feel better.

q.q: What is wrong with me?
Who takes me to the doctor?
What does the doctor say?

1.text: On Saturday I go to the market with Grandpa. We see red tomatoes and green peas. A man sells fresh fish. A woman sells yellow corn. Grandpa buys some fruit for me. I say, "Thank you!" He smiles.

q.q: Who goes to the market with me?
What does the woman sell?
What does Grandpa buy for me?

1.text: It is night on the farm. The cow is in the barn. The horse eats some hay. The hens sleep on their perches. A small owl sits in a tree. It says, "Hoo, hoo!" The farm is quiet. Good night, farm!

q.q: Where is the cow?
What does the horse eat?
Which animal says hoo?

1.text: I made a small robot with my dad. It is silver and has two blue eyes. It can walk and wave its hand. It can say, "Hello!" My little sister is afraid at first. Then she laughs and plays with it.

q.q: Who made the robot with me?
What colour are its eyes?
How is my sister at first?

1.text: It is Christmas morning. There is a green tree in our room. It has bright lights and shiny balls. Under the tree there are many gifts. I open a big red box. It is a new toy train! I say, "Thank you, Mum!"

q.q: What is in the red box?
What colour is the tree?
What is under the tree?

1.text: We live on the Earth. It is our home. We must keep it clean. Put your rubbish in the bin. Turn off the light when you leave a room. Plant a tree. Save water. Small things can help our big Earth.

q.q: Where do we put rubbish?
What should we do when we leave a room?
What can we plant?

2.text: I have a cat. Her name is Momo. She is small and white. She likes milk and fish. Every morning, Momo jumps on my bed. She says, "Meow!" I say, "Good morning, Momo!" I love my cat very much.

q.q: What is the cat's name?
What colour is Momo?
What does Momo do every morning?

2.text: It is a rainy day. The sky is grey. Tom has a red umbrella. He puts on his yellow boots. He jumps in the puddles. Splash! Splash! His mother laughs. "Come home, Tom. Let us drink hot tea," she says. Tom is wet but happy.

q.q: What colour is Tom's umbrella?
Where does Tom jump?
What does his mother want to drink?

2.text: Lily goes to school by bus. Her class starts at eight o'clock. First, they have an English lesson. Then they have art. Lily draws a big sun. At noon, she eats lunch with her friends. She likes rice and chicken. School is fun.

q.q: How does Lily go to school?
What does Lily draw?
What does she eat at noon?

2.text: Max is a hungry brown dog. He finds a big bone in the kitchen. He runs to the garden. He digs a hole and puts the bone inside. Then he covers it with dirt. Later, he cannot remember where it is. Poor Max! He looks everywhere.

q.q: Where does Max find the bone?
What does Max do in the garden?
Why is Max poor at the end?
q.a: He cannot remember where the bone is

2.text: It snowed last night. The garden is white. Ben and his sister make a snowman. They use a carrot for the nose and two stones for the eyes. Ben puts his hat on the snowman. It is cold, but they feel warm and happy. The snowman smiles at them.

q.q: What do they use for the nose?
What do they use for the eyes?
Who puts a hat on the snowman?

2.text: A crow has a piece of cheese. A fox sees it. He says, "You have a beautiful voice. Please sing!" The crow opens her mouth to sing. The cheese falls down. The fox eats it. The crow is sad. Do not trust sweet words.

q.q: What does the crow have?
Why does the crow open her mouth?
What is the lesson?

2.text: There are five people in my family. My father is a driver. My mother is a nurse. My brother is ten years old. My grandmother lives with us. She makes the best dumplings. On Sunday, we all eat dinner together. I love my family.

q.q: How many people are in the family?
What is the mother's job?
What does grandmother make?

2.text: We go to the beach on Saturday. The sun is hot and the water is blue. My dad builds a sandcastle with me. My little sister finds a shell. A crab walks past our feet! We all laugh. At night, we are tired and sleepy.

q.q: When do they go to the beach?
What does the little sister find?
How do they feel at night?

2.text: The sun shines in the day. It gives us light and heat. The moon comes out at night. The moon does not make light. It shines because the sun lights it. Stars are very far away. We can see them on clear nights.

q.q: What does the sun give us?
Why does the moon shine?
When can we see stars well?

2.text: Spring is here. Grandpa and I plant seeds in the garden. We water them every day. After two weeks, small green leaves come out. Later, red flowers open. Bees and butterflies come to visit. Grandpa smiles. "Plants need sun, water and love," he says.

q.q: Who plants seeds with the child?
What colour are the flowers?
What do plants need?

2.text: Today is Amy's birthday. She is seven. Her friends come to her house. They bring presents and sing a song. Amy blows out the candles and makes a wish. The cake is sweet and round. Everyone eats a piece. Amy says, "Thank you, my friends!"

q.q: How old is Amy?
What do the friends bring?
What does Amy do with the candles?

2.text: A hare laughs at a slow tortoise. "Let us have a race," says the tortoise. The hare runs fast. Then he sleeps under a tree. The tortoise walks and walks. He does not stop. He wins the race! Slow and steady wins.

q.q: Who wants a race?
Where does the hare sleep?
Who wins?

2.text: Chinese New Year is a big festival. Before the day, we clean the house. We hang red lanterns on the door. On New Year's Eve, the family eats dinner together. Children get red envelopes with money inside. At night, we watch fireworks in the sky. It is a happy time.

q.q: What do we do before the day?
What is inside the red envelopes?
What do we watch at night?

2.text: Today our class visits the zoo. We see a tall giraffe. It eats leaves from a tree. The monkeys jump and play. The lion sleeps in the shade. My favourite animal is the panda. It eats bamboo all day. I take many photos.

q.q: What does the giraffe eat?
Where does the lion sleep?
w: On a rock in the sun

q.q: What is the child's favourite animal?

2.text: Good teeth are important. Brush your teeth in the morning and at night. Use a soft brush and a little toothpaste. Brush for two minutes. Do not eat too many sweets. Go to the dentist twice a year. Then you will have a bright, healthy smile.

q.q: How long should you brush?
When should you brush?
q.a: In the morning and at night

q.q: How often should you see the dentist?

2.text: Mia has a red balloon. The wind blows hard. The balloon flies out of her hand! Mia is sad and cries. Then her friend Jack gives her a blue balloon. "Let us hold it together," he says. Mia smiles. They share the balloon all afternoon.

q.q: Why does the balloon fly away?
What colour is Jack's balloon?
How does Mia feel at the end?

2.text: Bees live in a hive. A hive is like a small house. Worker bees fly to flowers and drink sweet juice called nectar. They make honey from it. One bee makes only a little honey in its life. When you eat honey, think of the busy bees.

q.q: Where do bees live?
What is nectar?
How much honey does one bee make?

2.text: A little red hen finds some wheat. "Who will help me plant it?" she asks. "Not I," say the dog, the cat and the duck. So she plants it alone. Later, she makes bread. "Who will help me eat it?" "I will!" they say. "No," says the hen. "I will eat it myself."
2.src: adapted from the traditional folk tale The Little Red Hen (public domain)

q.q: What does the hen find?
Who helps her plant it?
Who eats the bread?

2.text: On Sunday, I go to the park with my dad. We fly a kite. The kite goes high into the sky. Then we play football. I kick the ball very far. Dad runs after it. We drink water and rest on the grass. I like sports. They make me strong.

q.q: Who goes to the park with the child?
What do they do first?
What do they do on the grass?

2.text: The Earth is our home. It has land and water. Most of the Earth is water. Plants, animals and people live here. We must keep it clean. Do not throw rubbish on the ground. Turn off lights when you leave a room. Small things can help our Earth.

q.q: What is most of the Earth?
What should we not do?
What is the main idea?
q.a: We can help the Earth by small things

2.text: In summer, an ant works hard. He carries food to his home. A grasshopper sings and plays all day. "Why do you work?" he asks. "Winter is coming," says the ant. Winter comes. The grasshopper has no food. He is cold and hungry. The ant gives him some food.

q.q: What does the ant do in summer?
Why is the grasshopper hungry?
What does the ant do at the end?
q.a: He gives food to the grasshopper

2.text: I have a toy robot. It is silver and it has two blue eyes. I press a button and it walks. It can say hello and sing a song. A battery makes it move. When the battery is empty, the robot stops. Then my dad puts in a new one. Robot is my best toy.

q.q: What colour are the robot's eyes?
What makes the robot move?
Who puts in a new battery?

2.text: China is a big country. In the north, it is cold in winter. In the south, it is warm. The Yellow River and the Yangtze River are two long rivers. There are tall mountains in the west. Beijing is the capital city. Many people visit the Great Wall.

q.q: What is the weather like in the south in winter?
Where are the tall mountains?
What is Beijing?

2.text: Shopkeeper: What do you want, Ben? Ben: I want some apples, please. Shopkeeper: How many? Ben: Three, please. Shopkeeper: Here you are. That is six yuan. Ben: Thank you! Shopkeeper: You are welcome. Go home and wash the apples first.

q.q: What does Ben want?
How many does he buy?
What should Ben do at home?

2.text: The wind and the sun see a man in a coat. "I can take off his coat," says the wind. The wind blows hard. The man holds his coat tight. Then the sun shines warm. The man feels hot and takes off his coat. The sun wins. Kind ways are better than strong ways.

q.q: What does the wind want to do?
What does the man do when the wind blows?
Who wins?

2.text: Dad puts on a funny hat. It is big and green. It has a long feather. "Do I look good?" he asks. My sister laughs and laughs. The dog barks at the hat. Even Mum cannot stop laughing. "It is my hat!" says Mum. Dad goes red.

q.q: What colour is the hat?
Who barks at the hat?
Whose hat is it?

2.text: We take a train to see Grandpa. The train is long and fast. I sit by the window and look at the fields. I see cows, rivers and small houses. A man sells snacks. My brother sleeps on my shoulder. After three hours, we arrive. Grandpa waves at us at the station.

q.q: Who do they visit?
What does the child see from the window?
How long is the trip?

2.text: Children need ten hours of sleep every night. When we sleep, our body rests and grows. Our brain also keeps what we learned that day. If we do not sleep enough, we feel tired and cannot think well. Turn off the phone early, read a book, and go to bed on time.

q.q: How much sleep do children need?
What does the brain do while we sleep?
What should you do before bed?
q.a: Turn off the phone and read

2.text: A boy looks after sheep on a hill. He is bored. "Wolf! Wolf!" he shouts. The farmers run to help, but there is no wolf. The boy laughs. He does this again. One day, a real wolf comes. The boy shouts, but nobody comes. The sheep run away. Nobody believes a liar.

q.q: Why does the boy shout the first time?
Why does nobody come at the end?
What is the lesson?

2.text: Giant pandas live in the mountains of Sichuan. They eat bamboo for about twelve hours a day. A baby panda is tiny, pink and has no fur at first. Today there are more pandas than before, because people protect the forests where they live.

q.q: What do pandas eat?
What does a baby panda look like?
q.a: Tiny and pink with no fur

q.q: Why are there more pandas now?

2.text: Where does rain come from? The sun warms the water in rivers and seas. The water goes up into the air as a gas that we cannot see. High in the sky, it gets cold and turns into tiny drops. Many drops make a cloud. When the drops get heavy, they fall as rain.

q.q: What warms the water?
What makes a cloud?
When does rain fall?

2.text: The Dragon Boat Festival is in early summer. People remember a poet named Qu Yuan, who loved his country. On this day, families eat zongzi, rice wrapped in leaves. In many places, teams row long boats that look like dragons. Drums beat and people cheer. It is exciting to watch.

q.q: Who do people remember on this day?
What is zongzi?
What do the long boats look like?

2.text: Helen cannot find her house key. She looks in her bag and in her pockets. She asks her teacher and her friends. At last, her little brother laughs. "It is on your neck!" he says. Helen puts her hand up. The key hangs on a string around her neck. Everyone laughs together.

q.q: What cannot Helen find?
Who finds the key?
Where is the key?
q.a: On a string around her neck

2.text: Our school team practises football on Tuesday and Thursday. Coach Wang tells us to pass the ball, not to keep it. At first, I do not like this. Then we win our first match because everyone works together. I learn that a team is stronger than one player.

q.q: When does the team practise?
What does the coach want the players to do?
What does the child learn?
q.a: A team is stronger than one player

2.text: A lion catches a little mouse. "Please let me go," says the mouse. "One day I will help you." The lion laughs but lets him go. Later, hunters catch the lion in a net. The mouse hears him roar. He bites the net with his small teeth, and the lion is free. Small friends can be great friends.

q.q: What does the mouse ask the lion?
How do hunters catch the lion?
w: With a rope on his leg

q.q: How does the mouse help?

2.text: At our school, we put paper, plastic and glass in different bins. Trucks take them to a factory. There, old paper becomes new paper, and old bottles can become new ones. This saves trees, water and energy. Last month our class collected fifty bottles. We are proud of our small job.

q.q: Where do trucks take the rubbish for recycling?
What does recycling save?
How many bottles did the class collect?

2.text: In autumn, the moon is round and bright. On Mid-Autumn Festival, families get together. We eat mooncakes and look at the moon. Grandma tells the story of Chang'e, a lady who flew to the moon. Children carry lanterns in the park. I like the sweet lotus seed mooncakes best.

q.q: What season is the festival in?
Who tells the story of Chang'e?
Which mooncake does the child like best?

2.text: Tom: Hello, Jack. This is Tom. Are you free tomorrow? Jack: Yes, I am. Why? Tom: Let us ride our bikes to the lake. Jack: Great idea! What time? Tom: At nine. I will bring water. Jack: And I will bring some bread. See you tomorrow!

q.q: Where do the boys want to go?
What time do they go?
What will Jack bring?

2.text: Thomas Edison was an American inventor. As a boy, he loved to ask questions and try things. He made many machines, and he improved the electric light so that people could use it at home. He tried hundreds of materials before he found one that worked well. He never stopped trying.

q.q: What was Edison?
What did he improve?
What is the main idea?
q.a: He kept trying until it worked

2.text: Sam and his uncle walk in the forest. It is quiet and cool. Tall trees make big shadows on the ground. Uncle shows him a bird's nest on a branch. Three small eggs are inside. "Do not touch them," says Uncle. "The mother bird will come back." They watch from far away until she lands on the nest.

q.q: Who walks with Sam?
How many eggs are in the nest?
Why should they not touch the eggs?
q.a: The mother bird will come back

2.text: Plants cannot walk, but their seeds can travel. A dandelion seed has soft white hairs, and the wind carries it far away. Some seeds have hooks and stick to an animal's fur. Birds eat sweet fruit and drop the seeds in new places. In this way, plants find new homes.

q.q: What carries a dandelion seed?
How do seeds with hooks travel?
What is the main idea?
q.a: Seeds have many ways to travel

2.text: The Great Wall of China is very long. People built it over many hundreds of years to keep out enemies. It goes over mountains and through deserts. Some parts are old and broken, but other parts are still strong. Every year, millions of visitors walk on it. Many of them take photos of the beautiful view.

q.q: Why did people build the wall?
Where does the wall go?
What do many visitors do?

2.text: Our teacher says, "This week is Kindness Week." Each child must do one kind thing every day. Lucy helps a little boy find his lost cap. Peter shares his lunch with a new girl. I clean the board for our teacher. On Friday, we feel proud. Being kind also makes you happy.

q.q: What does Lucy help find?
Who shares his lunch?
What does the narrator do?

2.t: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
2.text: A town mouse visits his friend in the country. They eat simple food, but the country mouse is happy. Then the country mouse visits the town. The food there is rich, but a cat chases them. "I want to go home," says the country mouse. "Simple food and no fear is better."

q.q: Who visits the country first?
What happens in the town?
What does the country mouse prefer?

2.text: To stay healthy, we should move our bodies every day. You can run, swim, skip or dance. Try to play outside for one hour. Eat fruit and vegetables, and drink water, not too much juice. After exercise, you may feel hot and out of breath. That is normal. Rest for a few minutes, and then you will be fine.

q.q: How long should you play outside?
What should you drink?
What should you do if you are out of breath?

2.text: Our class visits a museum of history. We see old coins, clay pots and a big bronze bell. The guide says some things are more than two thousand years old. In one room, there is a model of an ancient village. I wonder how people lived without electricity or phones. I want to come again.

q.q: What is the bell made of?
How old are some things?
What does the child wonder?

2.text: A thirsty crow finds a jug with a little water at the bottom. His beak is too short to reach it. He thinks hard. Then he picks up small stones and drops them into the jug, one by one. The water slowly rises. At last, the crow can drink. Clever thinking is better than strength.

q.q: Why can the crow not drink at first?
What does the crow drop into the jug?
What is the lesson?
q.a: Clever thinking is better than strength

2.text: Our class makes a weather chart. Each morning, one child looks at the sky and checks the thermometer. We write down if it is sunny, cloudy, windy or rainy. At the end of the month, we count the days. This month had twelve sunny days and only four rainy days. Our chart helps us understand the weather.

q.q: When does a child check the weather?
How many rainy days were there?
What does the chart help us do?

2.text: Grandma has a new smartphone. She cannot use it well. She presses the wrong button and calls the baker at midnight. Then she takes forty photos of her own thumb. We teach her how to send a message. Now she sends us a picture of her dinner every day. Sometimes it is only a blurry spoon!

q.q: Who does Grandma call by mistake?
What does she photograph forty times?
What does she send every day now?

2.text: Long ago, traders carried silk from China to faraway lands. They travelled with camels along a long road called the Silk Road. The trip took many months and was often dangerous. Traders also sold tea, spices and paper. They shared new ideas and stories, too. Because of this road, people in different countries learned about each other.

q.q: What animals did traders use?
How long did the trip take?
What else did traders share?

2.text: Helen Keller was born in America in 1880. When she was a baby, she became ill and could not see or hear. Her teacher, Anne Sullivan, taught her words by spelling them into her hand. Helen learned to read and write, and she went to university. Later, she travelled the world and helped many people.

q.q: What happened to Helen as a baby?
q.a: She became ill and could not see or hear

q.q: How did Anne Sullivan teach Helen?
q.a: By spelling words into her hand

q.q: What did Helen do later?

2.text: It is the last week of the year. Our class looks back at what we did. We learned new words and made new friends. Kim can now ride a bike. Jo can swim. I can read a long book alone. Our teacher says, "You grew a lot this year." Now we look forward to new dreams.

q.q: What can Kim do now?
What can the narrator do?
What does the teacher say?
q.a: You grew a lot this year

3.text: I have a cat. Her name is Mimi. She is small and white. She has green eyes and a long tail. Mimi likes milk and fish. She sleeps on my bed every night. In the morning, she jumps on my desk and says, "Meow!" I give her some food. Then we play with a red ball. I love my cat very much.

q.q: What colour is Mimi?
What does Mimi like?
Where does Mimi sleep?

3.text: It is spring. The weather is warm and the sun is bright. Flowers are open in the park. Pink and yellow flowers are everywhere. Birds are singing in the trees. Some children are flying kites. Others are riding bikes on the grass. Amy and her mum are walking by the lake. They are very happy. Spring is a beautiful season.

q.q: What are the birds doing?
What are some children flying?
Who is walking by the lake?

3.text: A big lion is sleeping under a tree. A little mouse runs over his face. The lion wakes up. He is angry. "Please, don't eat me," says the mouse. "One day I can help you." The lion laughs, but he lets her go. Later, a hunter catches the lion in a net. The mouse bites the net and he is free.

q.q: Where is the lion sleeping?
Who catches the lion?
How does the mouse help the lion?

3.text: There are five people in my family. My father is a doctor. He works in a big hospital. My mother is a teacher. She teaches English. My grandmother lives with us. She is kind and she can cook very well. I have a little brother, too. His name is Ben. He is three years old. We are a happy family.

q.q: What is the father's job?
Who can cook very well?
How old is Ben?

3.text: Lily goes to school at seven thirty. Her first class is Chinese. Then she has maths and music. At twelve o'clock, she eats lunch with her friends. After lunch, they play in the playground. Lily likes art class best. She can draw flowers and animals. School finishes at four o'clock. Then Lily goes home by bus.

q.q: What is Lily's first class?
What does Lily like best?
How does Lily go home?

3.text: "Good morning," says Mr Wang. "Can I help you?" Tina wants some fruit. "I would like three apples and two bananas, please," she says. "Here you are," says Mr Wang. "Anything else?" "Yes, I like grapes. How much are they?" "They are ten yuan." "OK, I'll take them. Thank you!" Tina pays and goes home with a full bag.

q.q: What does Tina want first?
How much are the grapes?
Who sells the fruit?

3.text: Pandas live in China. They are black and white and they are very cute. A panda eats bamboo for about twelve hours every day. It is big, but it can climb trees well. Baby pandas are very small. They are pink at first! Many people visit Chengdu to see pandas. Do you like pandas? I do.

q.q: What do pandas eat?
What colour are baby pandas at first?
Where can people see pandas?

3.text: My friends have different hobbies. Jack likes playing football. He plays every Saturday. Mary likes reading books. She reads a story every night. Sam can sing and dance. He is in the school music club. My hobby is swimming. I swim twice a week. What is your hobby? Tell me about it!

q.q: What does Jack like?
When does Mary read a story?
What can Sam do?

3.text: It is raining today. The sky is grey and the streets are wet. Mike cannot play outside. He is at home with his sister. They are playing a board game on the floor. Mum is making hot soup in the kitchen. It smells good! Mike looks out of the window. "I hope it is sunny tomorrow," he says.

q.q: What is the weather like?
What is Mum making?
What are Mike and his sister playing?

3.text: The Mid-Autumn Festival is in autumn. On this night, the moon is big and round. Families eat dinner together. Children eat sweet moon cakes. Some moon cakes have eggs inside. People look at the moon and talk. Grandpa tells a story about a lady who lives on the moon. Everyone is happy.

q.q: When is the Mid-Autumn Festival?
What do children eat?
Who tells a story?

3.text: This is my bedroom. It is small, but I like it. There is a bed near the window. There is a desk next to the bed. On the desk, there are some books and a lamp. I have a toy box under the bed. A big map of the world is on the wall. I read and do my homework here.

q.q: Where is the bed?
What is under the bed?
What is on the wall?

3.text: A hare laughs at a slow tortoise. "I can run much faster than you," he says. "Let's have a race," says the tortoise. They start. The hare runs fast and soon he is far away. He thinks, "I can sleep now." He lies down under a tree. The tortoise walks and walks. He does not stop. The tortoise wins the race!

q.q: Who is slow?
Why does the hare sleep?
q.a: He thinks he is far ahead.

q.q: Who wins the race?

3.text: Summer is hot, but I love it. School is closed for two months. Every morning, I get up late. My family goes to the beach. We swim in the sea and eat ice cream. My dad makes a big sandcastle. At night, we watch the stars. I take many photos. I want a longer summer!

q.q: Where does the family go?
What does Dad make?
What do they watch at night?

3.text: Bobby is a brown dog. He lives on a farm. He has big ears and a short tail. Every day, he runs with the sheep. He barks at strangers. Bobby likes bones and he loves swimming in the river. In the evening, he is tired. He lies by the door and goes to sleep. He is a good dog.

q.q: Where does Bobby live?
What does Bobby run with?
What does Bobby love?

3.text: Tom has good habits. He gets up early and washes his face. He eats breakfast every day. He likes eggs and milk. He does not eat too many sweets. After school, he plays sports for one hour. He goes to bed at nine o'clock. Tom is strong and healthy. Can you be like Tom?

q.q: What does Tom eat for breakfast?
How long does Tom play sports?
When does Tom go to bed?

3.text: A little bird lives in a tree near my house. Her wings are blue. She cannot fly high yet. Every day, she tries again and again. I watch her from my window. One sunny morning, she jumps from a branch and flies to the roof! "Well done!" I shout. She sings a happy song. Never give up!

q.q: What colour are the bird's wings?
Where does the bird fly to?
What is the main idea?

3.text: Our class has a pet rabbit. Its name is Snow. It is white and soft. Every day, two students feed it with carrots and grass. Snow likes to hop around the classroom. When we are noisy, it hides in its house. Today is my turn to clean its home. I am happy because I love Snow.

q.q: What is the rabbit's name?
What does the rabbit eat?
What does it do when children are noisy?

3.text: On Sunday, we visit the zoo. First, we see the monkeys. They are funny and they eat bananas. Then we see the elephants. They are very big and they have long noses. I like the penguins best. They walk in a funny way and swim fast. We have a picnic under a tree. It is a great day!

q.q: What do the monkeys eat?
Which animal does the writer like best?
What do they do under the tree?

3.text: It is winter and it is very cold. Snow is falling from the sky. The mountains and houses are white. Ben puts on his hat, scarf and gloves. He goes outside with his sister. They make a snowman. It has a carrot nose and two black eyes. Then they drink hot chocolate at home.

q.q: What is falling from the sky?
What is the snowman's nose?
What do they drink at home?

3.text: Spring Festival is the biggest festival in China. Before the festival, families clean their houses. They put red paper on the doors. On New Year's Eve, everyone eats dumplings together. Children get red envelopes with money inside. People wear new clothes and visit their friends. Fireworks fill the night sky. Happy New Year!

q.q: What do families eat on New Year's Eve?
What do children get?
What fills the night sky?

3.text: A boy looks after sheep on a hill. He is bored. "Wolf! Wolf!" he shouts. The farmers run to help, but there is no wolf. The boy laughs. He does it again, and again the farmers come. One day, a real wolf comes. "Wolf! Wolf!" shouts the boy. But nobody comes, because they think he is joking.

q.q: What does the boy look after?
Why does nobody come at last?
What is the boy at first?

3.text: I visit Grandma every weekend. She lives in a small village. Her house has a big garden. She grows tomatoes, beans and flowers. I help her water the plants. Grandma can make the best noodles in the world. We eat lunch under an old apple tree. Then she tells me stories about her childhood.

q.q: Where does Grandma live?
What does Grandma grow?
Where do they eat lunch?

3.text: At night, I look up at the sky. The moon is bright and the stars are small, shiny points of light. The moon does not make its own light. It shines because the sun lights it. The moon looks different on different nights. Sometimes it is a thin line. Sometimes it is a big circle. I love the night sky.

q.q: Why does the moon shine?
What does the moon look like sometimes?
What are the stars like?

3.text: Today is Sports Day at our school. The sun is shining and everyone is excited. Some students run in the one hundred metre race. Others jump in the long jump. My class is in the tug-of-war. We pull the rope very hard. We win! Our teacher claps and smiles. After the games, we get small medals. I am proud of my team.

q.q: What is the weather like?
Which game does the writer's class play?
What do the students get after the games?

3.text: Lucy cannot find her umbrella. It is yellow with small blue dots. "Is it in your bag?" asks Mum. "No," says Lucy. "Is it under the sofa?" "No, it isn't." Then Dad laughs. "Look at the door!" The yellow umbrella is behind the door. Lucy smiles. "Thank you, Dad!" she says. Now she can go to school.

q.q: What colour is the umbrella?
Where is the umbrella?
Who finds it?

3.text: Mr Green is a postman. He gets up at five o'clock every morning. He rides his bike and delivers letters to many houses. He knows everyone in the town. When it rains, he wears a yellow coat. Old people like him because he says hello with a big smile. He is a friendly man and a great helper.

q.q: What is Mr Green's job?
What does he wear when it rains?
Why do old people like him?

3.text: The Dragon Boat Festival is in early summer. People remember a poet called Qu Yuan. On this day, families make zongzi. These are sticky rice parcels in green leaves. They can have meat, beans or dates inside. In many rivers, teams race in long boats shaped like dragons. Drummers sit at the front and everyone paddles together. The crowd cheers loudly.

q.q: What do families make?
What shape are the boats?
Who sits at the front?

3.text: A hungry fox walks in the forest. He sees some sweet grapes on a high vine. "They look delicious," he says. He jumps, but he cannot reach them. He jumps again and again. At last he is tired. "Those grapes are probably sour," he says, and walks away. Some people also say bad things about what they cannot have.

q.q: What does the fox want?
Why does he walk away?
What does the fox say at the end?

3.text: Honey bees live in groups called colonies. One colony can have thousands of bees. The queen lays the eggs. Worker bees fly from flower to flower and collect sweet nectar. They carry it back to the hive and make honey. Bees also dance to show other bees where the flowers are. Bees are small, but they are very useful.

q.q: Who lays the eggs?
Why do bees dance?
What do worker bees collect?

3.text: Today is Anna's tenth birthday. She wakes up and the house is quiet. "Maybe everyone forgets," she thinks. She goes to the living room. Suddenly, her family and friends jump out. "Happy birthday!" they shout. There are balloons on the walls and a big chocolate cake on the table. Anna cannot stop smiling. She makes a wish and blows out the candles.

q.q: How old is Anna?
What does Anna think at first?
What is on the table?

3.text: The Great Wall is one of the longest walls in the world. It is thousands of kilometres long and it goes over mountains and through deserts. People built it a very long time ago to keep enemies out. Today, millions of visitors walk on it every year. From the top, you can see green hills and small villages. It is a symbol of China.

q.q: Why did people build the Great Wall?
What can you see from the top?
What is the Great Wall a symbol of?

3.text: Tina learns chess with her grandpa. At first, she does not know the pieces. Grandpa shows her the king, the queen and the horse. "Think before you move," he says. Tina plays slowly and carefully. She loses the first ten games, but she keeps learning. Now she sometimes wins. Grandpa is proud. "You are a clever girl," he says.

q.q: Who teaches Tina chess?
What does Grandpa say?
How is Tina now?

3.text: The sun warms the sea, rivers and lakes. Some water turns into a gas and goes up into the air. High in the sky, it is cold. The gas becomes tiny drops of water and makes clouds. When the drops get big and heavy, they fall down as rain. The water goes back to the rivers and the sea. Then it starts again.

q.q: What warms the water?
What makes clouds?
What is the main idea?

3.text: Dear Emma, how are you? I am writing from my uncle's farm in Wales. It is a beautiful place. In the morning, I feed the chickens and collect eggs. In the afternoon, I ride a horse. The horse is called Star. It is very gentle. The evenings are quiet, and I read by the fire. I miss you. Please write soon. Love, Kate

q.q: Where is Kate?
What does Kate do in the afternoon?
What is the horse like?

3.text: A mother duck has six eggs. Five ducklings come out, small and yellow. The last one is big and grey. The other animals laugh at him. "You are ugly!" they say. The little bird feels sad and runs away. He spends a cold winter alone. In spring, he sees his face in the water. He is not a duck. He is a beautiful white swan!
3.src: adapted from Hans Christian Andersen (public domain)

q.q: What colour is the last duckling?
Why does he run away?
What is he in the end?

3.text: This week, our school is collecting rubbish for recycling. We put paper, plastic and glass into different boxes. Mr Lee says that we can make new things from old ones. Last year, our class collected fifty kilos of paper! We also bring our own bags to the shop. Small actions help our planet. We want a clean and green world.

q.q: What do students put in different boxes?
How much paper did the class collect?
What does the school want?

3.text: Ming has a new kite. It is shaped like a big red fish. On a windy afternoon, he goes to the park with his father. Dad holds the kite high and Ming runs. The wind catches it and the fish flies up into the sky. Ming holds the string tightly. "Look, it is swimming in the clouds!" he laughs. They fly it until the sun goes down.

q.q: What shape is the kite?
What is the weather like?
Who goes to the park with Ming?

3.text: Dr Li works in a small town hospital. Every day, many children come to see her. She does not wear a scary white coat. She wears a colourful one with cartoon animals. First, she talks and jokes with the children. Then she checks their throats and ears. Her young patients are not afraid. "She is the best doctor," they say.

q.q: Where does Dr Li work?
What is special about her coat?
What does she do first?

3.text: In my town, there are four seasons. Spring is green and rainy. Summer is hot and long. In autumn, the leaves turn red and yellow and fall from the trees. Winter is cold and sometimes snowy. I like autumn best because the weather is cool. I can collect leaves and make pictures with them. Which season do you like?

q.q: Which season is hot and long?
What happens to leaves in autumn?
Why does the writer like autumn?

3.text: In a Chinese story, Monkey King lives on a mountain. One day, he goes into a garden in the sky. There are many magic peaches. They can make a person live for a very long time. Monkey is hungry, so he eats and eats. The guards find him and he runs away fast. Monkey laughs, "They are the best peaches I have ever eaten!"
3.src: adapted from Chinese folk tales (public domain)

q.q: Where is the garden?
What can the peaches do?
What does Monkey do when the guards come?

3.text: Every Tuesday and Thursday, Jim practises football after school. His coach is Mr Brown. First, the boys run around the field. Then they pass the ball in pairs. Jim can kick very well with his left foot. Today, he scores two goals in a small game. "Good job!" says Mr Brown. Jim feels happy and a little tired, but he loves football.

q.q: When does Jim practise?
Who is Mr Brown?
How many goals does Jim score?

3.text: The sea is home to millions of animals. Small fish swim in groups to stay safe. Crabs walk sideways on the sand. Dolphins are not fish. They are mammals, so they breathe air and need to come up to the top of the water. Whales are the biggest animals on Earth. Some are as long as three buses. The sea is full of life.

q.q: How do crabs walk?
Why do dolphins come to the top?
What are the biggest animals on Earth?

3.text: A long time ago in China, Emperor Shennong boils water under a tree. A few leaves fall into the pot. The water turns brown and smells nice. He drinks it and likes it. People say this is how tea began. Today, tea is one of the most popular drinks in the world. Chinese families drink it every day and offer it to guests.

q.q: What falls into the pot?
What happens to the water?
Who drinks tea every day?

3.text: Sara is new at school. She stands alone at lunch time. Mia sees her and says, "Hello! Do you want to sit with us?" Sara smiles. They talk about their favourite things. Both girls like drawing and cats. After lunch, they go to the art room together. Sara is not sad now. "I have a friend," she tells her mum that night.

q.q: Why does Sara stand alone?
What do both girls like?
Who invites Sara to sit?

3.text: Our family goes camping near a quiet lake. Dad puts up the tent and I help him. In the afternoon, we fish and swim. Mum cooks sausages on a small fire. After dinner, we sit and sing songs. At night, I can see a thousand stars. Sometimes an owl calls from the trees. I sleep well in my warm sleeping bag.

q.q: Who puts up the tent?
What does Mum cook?
What calls from the trees?

3.text: One rainy morning, Jack walks to school with a big umbrella. He sees an old woman at the bus stop. She has no umbrella and her coat is wet. Jack thinks for a moment. Then he walks to her and says, "You can use mine." The woman smiles. "Thank you, kind boy." Jack gets wet, but his heart feels warm.

q.q: Where does Jack see the old woman?
What does Jack do?
How does Jack feel at the end?

3.text: A shadow appears when something blocks the light. On a sunny day, you have a shadow too. In the morning, it is long. At noon, when the sun is high, your shadow is short. In the evening, it becomes long again. You can play with shadows at home. Shine a torch on your hand and make a rabbit on the wall.

q.q: When is your shadow short?
What makes a shadow?
What can you make with a torch?

3.text: Four friends climb a hill on Saturday. Tom walks fast and goes first. Kim is slow because she carries a heavy bag. "Let me help you," says Tom, and he takes the bag. Then they climb together and reach the top at noon. They sit on the grass and share sandwiches. The view is wonderful. "It is better to arrive together," says Kim.

q.q: Why is Kim slow?
What does Tom do?
What do they share?

3.text: Paper cutting is an old Chinese art. People use scissors to cut pictures from red paper. Flowers, fish, animals and the Chinese word for luck are popular shapes. At Spring Festival, families stick them on windows to bring good luck. Grandma Zhao is very good at it. She folds the paper and cuts quickly. Then she opens it, and a beautiful flower appears!

q.q: What colour is the paper?
Where do families stick the pictures?
What does Grandma Zhao cut at the end?

3.text: Every Friday, I go to the robot club. We have small kits with wheels, wires and a little computer. Last week, my team built a robot car. It can move forward and turn left or right. We use a tablet to control it. Today, we want it to stop when it meets a wall. It is not easy, but we are learning. Making things is fun.

q.q: When is the robot club?
What can the robot car do?
What does the team want today?
q.a: The car stops at a wall.

3.text: One morning, Lena looks out of the window. Everything is white! Snow lies on the roofs, cars and trees. "No school today!" says her dad, reading the news. Lena jumps with joy. She puts on her boots and runs into the garden. Her little brother and she roll a huge snowball for a snowman. Later, they sit by the warm fire and eat hot toast. What a lovely day!

q.q: Why is there no school?
What do the children make?
What do they eat later?

3.t: My Wishes for the New Year
3.text: The new year begins soon. I have three wishes. First, I want to read fifty books. I have a list on my desk and I tick every book I finish. Second, I would like to learn to swim well, so I go to the pool on Sundays. Third, I want to be kind to everyone. What are your wishes for the new year?

q.q: How many books does the writer want to read?
When does the writer go to the pool?
What is the third wish?

4.text: Last Saturday, Tom got a new bike for his birthday. It was red and very shiny. There were two bells on it. Tom was so happy that he rode it to the park at once. The park was bigger than his school yard, and there were many trees. He rode round the lake three times. Then he fell off and hurt his knee, but he was not sad. His father laughed and said, "Every good rider falls sometimes." Tom stood up and rode home slowly. It was the best birthday ever.

q.q: What colour was Tom's new bike?
Where did Tom ride his bike?
How did Tom feel at the end?

4.text: One hot day, a lion was sleeping under a tree. A little mouse ran over his nose and woke him up. The lion was angry and caught the mouse in his big paw. "Please let me go," said the mouse. "One day I will help you." The lion laughed, but he let the mouse go. A week later, hunters caught the lion in a net. He roared loudly. The mouse heard him and came quickly. She cut the net with her sharp teeth, and the lion was free. Small friends can be great friends.
4.src: adapted from The Lion and the Mouse, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why was the lion angry?
How did the mouse help the lion?
What is the main idea of the story?
q.a: Small friends can help big ones

4.text: It rained all day on Sunday, so Mia and her brother Ben stayed at home. There were many toys in the living room, but they wanted to do something new. Mia had an idea. "Let's build a castle with boxes!" she said. They found six big boxes and some paper. Ben painted the walls grey. Mia made a flag from a red sock. After two hours, the castle was taller than the sofa. Their mother took a photo of it. In the evening, the rain stopped, and the children went to bed happily.

q.q: Why did the children stay at home?
What did Mia use to make the flag?
How tall was the castle?

4.text: Cats make many sounds. The softest and nicest one is the purr. A cat usually purrs when it is happy, for example when you stroke it. But sometimes a cat purrs when it is ill or afraid. Scientists think the sound helps the cat feel calm. Baby cats begin to purr when they are only a few days old. They purr to tell their mother, "I am here and I am fine." A big lion cannot purr like a house cat, but it can roar much louder. Next time your cat purrs, listen carefully.

q.q: When does a cat usually purr?
What do baby cats tell their mother?
Which animal can roar louder than a house cat?

4.text: Lily is my best friend. She is nine years old, and she is a little taller than me. Her hair is long and black. She has a big smile and a loud laugh. Lily is good at drawing, but I am better at maths. We sit next to each other in class. At lunch, she shares her fruit with me, and I share my cakes with her. Last week I lost my pencil case. Lily gave me a new pencil. That was so kind. I hope we stay friends for ever.

q.q: Who is better at maths?
What did Lily give the writer?
What does "kind" mean here?

4.text: Chinese New Year is the most important holiday in China. Before the day, families clean their houses and buy new clothes. On New Year's Eve, everyone has a big dinner together. There are fish, dumplings and many other dishes. Children get red envelopes with money inside from their grandparents. At night, people watch fireworks in the sky. In many cities, there are dragon dances in the streets. The holiday lasts about fifteen days. It ends with the Lantern Festival, when people eat sweet rice balls and look at beautiful lanterns.

q.q: What do families do before the holiday?
Who gives children red envelopes?
How does the holiday end?

4.text: A poor woodcutter was cutting a tree by a river when his axe fell into the water. He sat down and cried. Suddenly, a kind spirit came out of the river. She showed him a gold axe. "Is this yours?" she asked. "No," said the man. She showed him a silver axe. "No," he said again. Then she showed him his old iron axe. "Yes, that is mine!" he said happily. The spirit was pleased with his honesty and gave him all three axes. He went home rich and happy.
4.src: adapted from The Honest Woodcutter, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: What fell into the river?
Which axe belonged to the man?
Why did the spirit give him three axes?

4.text: Last spring, our class made a small garden behind the school. First, we cleaned the ground and took out the stones. Then our teacher, Mr Green, gave us seeds. We planted carrots, beans and flowers in long rows. Every morning two children watered the plants. After one month, there were tiny green leaves everywhere. In summer, the beans were longer than my hand! We picked them and cooked them for lunch. They tasted much better than the beans from the shop. Now everyone in our school wants a garden at home too.

q.q: Where was the garden?
Who gave the children seeds?
How did the beans taste?

4.text: On Friday, Sam's class visited the zoo. There were more than two hundred animals there. First, they saw the elephants. An elephant is much bigger than a horse, and its nose is very long. Next, they watched the monkeys. The monkeys were funnier than the other animals. One monkey took a boy's hat and ran away! Everyone laughed. At twelve o'clock, the children ate lunch near the pandas. Sam liked the pandas best because they were so soft and slow. He bought a small panda toy for his sister before the bus took them home.

q.q: What did a monkey do?
Where did the children eat lunch?
What did Sam buy?

4.text: Water is always moving. The sun heats the sea, the rivers and the lakes. Some water turns into a gas and goes up into the sky. We cannot see this gas. High in the sky, it is much colder, so the gas turns into tiny drops of water. These drops make clouds. When the clouds get heavy, the drops fall down as rain. If it is very cold, they fall as snow. The rain fills the rivers, and the rivers run back to the sea. Then the story starts again. This is called the water cycle.

q.q: What heats the water?
Why does the gas turn into drops high in the sky?
What is the main idea?

4.text: Anna and her father went to the supermarket on Saturday morning. There was a long list in Dad's hand. "We need milk, eggs, apples and bread," he said. Anna pushed the trolley. In the fruit section, there were red apples and green apples. The green ones were cheaper, but Anna liked the red ones more, so they bought six red ones. Then they looked for the milk. "Excuse me, where is the milk?" Anna asked a worker. He smiled and pointed to the back. At the end, Dad paid, and Anna carried the lightest bag home.

q.q: What did Anna push?
Which apples were cheaper?
Who carried the lightest bag?

4.text: Marco Polo was born in Venice, Italy, about 770 years ago. When he was seventeen, he went with his father and uncle on a very long journey to Asia. They travelled for almost four years by ship, on horses and on foot. At last they arrived in China and met the great emperor Kublai Khan. Marco liked the emperor, and he stayed in China for many years. He saw paper money, black stones that burned, and big busy cities. Later, he wrote a book about his travels. Many people read it and wanted to see China too.

q.q: Where was Marco Polo born?
How did the family travel?
q.a: By ship, horse and on foot

q.q: What did Marco do after his trip?

4.text: It was a bright, warm day in May. Our class went to the river for a picnic. There were twenty-five children and three teachers. We walked for half an hour, and we were very hungry when we arrived. Everyone put a big blanket on the grass. We had sandwiches, fruit, juice and biscuits. After lunch, we played football and hide-and-seek. Jack found the best hiding place, behind a big rock. Nobody could find him for ten minutes! At four o'clock, we cleaned the grass and took our rubbish home. It was a lovely day.

q.q: How many teachers went on the picnic?
Where did Jack hide?
What did the children do at the end?

4.text: A hare laughed at a tortoise. "You are so slow!" he said. "Let's have a race," said the tortoise. The hare agreed, and the race began. The hare ran far ahead very quickly. Then he stopped under a tree. "I am much faster than he is," he thought. "I can sleep for a while." He fell asleep. The tortoise walked on and on, step by step. He did not stop once. When the hare woke up, the tortoise was already near the end. The hare ran as fast as he could, but it was too late. The tortoise won.
4.src: adapted from The Tortoise and the Hare, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why did the hare stop?
q.a: He thought he was fast enough

q.q: What did the tortoise do?
w: He ran faster than the hare

q.q: What is the main idea?

4.text: Last Monday, Emma had a sore throat and a high temperature. Her mother took her to the doctor. The waiting room was full, and there were many sick children. After twenty minutes, a nurse called Emma's name. The doctor looked at her throat and listened to her chest. "You have a cold," he said. "You must drink a lot of water, rest in bed and eat healthy food." He gave her some medicine, too. Emma stayed at home for three days. On Friday, she felt much better, and she went back to school with a big smile.

q.q: What was wrong with Emma?
What must Emma do?
When did Emma go back to school?

4.text: A mountain is much higher than a hill. The highest mountain in the world is Mount Everest. It is between China and Nepal, and it is almost nine kilometres high. It is so cold at the top that nobody can live there. In 1953, two men, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, were the first to climb it. Today, hundreds of people try every year, but it is a dangerous trip. There are also many beautiful mountains in China, for example Mount Tai and Huangshan. Some people go there to see the sunrise from the top.

q.q: Which is the highest mountain in the world?
Why can nobody live at the top?
What do some people do on Mount Tai?

4.text: One evening, Lucy found a small brown dog in front of her house. It was wet and cold, and it had no collar. "Poor dog," said Lucy. She gave it some water and a bit of chicken. Her father put up a note on the street: "Found: a small brown dog." Two days later, an old man came to the door. "That is my dog, Biscuit!" he said. Biscuit jumped into his arms and licked his face. The old man was so happy that he gave Lucy a bag of sweets. She smiled and said, "I am happy too."

q.q: What was the dog's name?
What did Lucy's father do?
w: He took the dog to a vet

q.q: Why did the old man give Lucy sweets?
q.a: He was happy to find his dog

4.text: Thousands of years ago, people lived without shops or houses like ours. There were no metal tools, so they made them from stone, wood and bone. A sharp stone could cut meat or make a hole in leather. People hunted animals and picked fruit and nuts. They lived in caves, and they used fire to keep warm and to cook. There was no writing, but they drew animals on the walls of caves. We can still see these pictures today. They tell us how people lived long, long ago and what animals they saw.

q.q: What did Stone Age people make tools from?
Where did they live?
What can we learn from the cave pictures?

4.text: Mother's Day was coming, and Kate wanted to surprise her mum. She asked her older brother Jim for help. "Let's make breakfast," he said. On Sunday, they got up at six o'clock. They were very quiet. Jim made some eggs, and Kate cut the bread and made tea. She also drew a big card with a red heart. Then they carried everything to Mum's room. Mum opened her eyes and could not believe it. "This is the best breakfast I ever had!" she said. She hugged her children for a long time. The eggs were a little burnt, but she ate them all.

q.q: What time did the children get up?
What did Kate draw?
What was wrong with the eggs?

4.text: Giant pandas live in the mountains of Sichuan, in south-west China. They are black and white, and they are bigger than most bears. A panda eats bamboo for about twelve hours every day. It eats more than ten kilograms! Baby pandas are very small. A new baby is smaller than a pencil case and has no black fur. It stays with its mother for about two years. There are not many wild pandas, so people protect them. In Chengdu, there is a big centre where visitors can watch pandas eat, climb and play.

q.q: What does a panda eat?
How is a new baby panda?
q.a: Very small with no black fur

q.q: Why do people protect pandas?
q.a: There are not many wild ones

4.text: On Saturday, our school team played football against Green School. The game was exciting. At first, the other team was stronger, and they scored a goal in ten minutes. Our captain, Leo, shouted, "Don't give up!" After the break, we played better. Leo passed the ball to Ming, and Ming kicked it into the net. It was one all! There were only two minutes left when Leo scored again. The crowd jumped and shouted. We won two to one. After the match, both teams shook hands. The other captain said, "You played well. See you next year!"

q.q: Who scored first?
What was the final score?
q.a: Two to one for our school
w: Two to one for Green School

q.q: What did both teams do after the match?

4.text: The moon is our nearest neighbour in space. It is much smaller than the Earth, and it has no air or water. During the day, it is very hot, and at night, it is extremely cold. The moon does not make its own light. We see it because it shines with light from the sun. Its shape seems to change from night to night. Sometimes it is round, and sometimes it is thin like a banana. In 1969, Neil Armstrong was the first man to walk on the moon. His footprints are still there, because there is no wind.

q.q: Does the moon make its own light?
w: No, it uses the Earth's light

q.q: Who was the first man on the moon?
Why are the footprints still there?
q.a: There is no wind on the moon

4.text: A shepherd boy looked after sheep on a hill near his village. He was bored, so he shouted, "Wolf! Wolf!" The villagers ran up the hill, but there was no wolf. The boy laughed at them. He did the same thing the next day. Again, the villagers came, and again there was no wolf. A few days later, a real wolf came. "Wolf! Wolf!" cried the boy. This time nobody came, because they thought he was lying. The wolf ate many sheep. The boy cried, "I was wrong. Now no one believes me."
4.src: adapted from The Boy Who Cried Wolf, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why did the boy shout "Wolf" the first time?
Why did nobody come the last time?
What is the main idea?

4.text: This weekend, I have a busy plan. On Saturday morning, I will go to my piano class at nine o'clock. After lunch, my cousin will come, and we will make a model plane. There are two hundred small parts in the box, so it will take a long time. In the evening, we will watch a film about dinosaurs. On Sunday, my family will go to my grandparents' farm. They have chickens, two cows and a very friendly dog. I will help Grandpa carry the water. I hope the weather is fine, because I love the farm.

q.q: What will the writer do on Saturday morning?
Who will make a model plane with the writer?
Where will the family go on Sunday?

4.text: Bees are small, but they work very hard. A bee flies from flower to flower and drinks a sweet juice called nectar. It carries the nectar back to its home, which is called a hive. There, the bees turn it into honey. One hive can have fifty thousand bees. Every bee has a job. Some bees clean the hive, some look after the babies, and some find flowers. When a bee finds good flowers, it does a special dance to tell the others where to go. Without bees, there would be fewer fruits and vegetables.

q.q: What is a bee's home called?
How does a bee tell others about good flowers?
Why are bees important?
q.a: They help fruits and vegetables grow

4.text: Last Sunday, I found an old photo in Grandpa's drawer. In the photo, there was a young boy in front of a small house. "Who is he?" I asked. Grandpa smiled and said, "That is me, sixty years ago." I could not believe it. The boy had a funny haircut and no shoes. "There was no school bus in my village," said Grandpa. "I walked to school every day, and the road was very long." He told me many stories about his childhood. Now I know that life was harder then, and I want to ask him more questions.

q.q: Where did the writer find the photo?
How did Grandpa go to school?
What does the writer want to do now?

4.text: One hot afternoon, a hungry fox walked through a garden. High above his head, he saw some big, purple grapes. "They look so sweet," he said. He jumped up, but he could not reach them. He tried again and again. He jumped from the left, then from the right, and then he ran and jumped as high as he could. At last, he was tired and sat down. "I don't want those grapes anyway," he said. "I am sure they are sour." Then he walked away with his nose in the air.
4.src: adapted from The Fox and the Grapes, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: What did the fox want?
Why did the fox say the grapes were sour?
What kind of animal is the fox in the story?
q.a: One who says he does not want what he cannot have

4.text: In July, the Wang family went to the beach for a holiday. The sea was warm and blue, and the sand was almost white. There were many people there, but it was not too noisy. Little Yu built a sandcastle with a deep hole around it. Her brother Hao swam far out, and their father shouted, "Come back! It is too deep!" At noon, they ate ice cream under a big umbrella. Then they looked for shells. Yu found twelve, and Hao found only seven. In the evening, they were tired, sunburnt and very happy.

q.q: Why did the father shout at Hao?
Who found more shells?
How did the family feel in the evening?

4.text: About two thousand years ago, merchants began to travel on a long road between China and Europe. We call it the Silk Road. They carried silk, tea and spices from the east, and horses, gold and glass from the west. The road was not one road but many paths through deserts and mountains. It was hot in the day, cold at night, and often dangerous. A trip could take a year. But the merchants did not only trade goods. They also shared ideas, music and stories. In this way, the people of different countries learned about each other.

q.q: What did merchants carry from China?
How long could a trip take?
What else did people share on the road?

4.text: How can we stay healthy? First, we should eat a balanced diet. That means eating vegetables, fruit, rice, fish and a little meat every day. We should drink water instead of fizzy drinks, because they have too much sugar. Second, we need exercise. Playing sport for one hour a day makes our hearts and bones stronger. Third, sleep is important. Children from nine to twelve years old need about ten hours a night. If you sleep late, you may feel tired at school. Finally, wash your hands often. These simple habits can make you feel great.

q.q: Why should we avoid fizzy drinks?
How much sleep do children aged nine to twelve need?
What is the main idea?

4.text: A mother duck had six eggs. Five of the ducklings were small and yellow, but the last one was big and grey. The other animals laughed at him. "You are so ugly!" they said. The poor duckling ran away and spent a cold winter alone near a frozen lake. When spring came, he saw some beautiful white birds on the water. He wanted to go near them, but he was afraid. He looked down and saw his face in the water. He was not an ugly duckling any more. He was a beautiful swan, and the other swans welcomed him.
4.src: adapted from The Ugly Duckling, Hans Christian Andersen (public domain)

q.q: What colour was the last duckling?
Why did the duckling run away?
What did the duckling find out in spring?

4.text: On Monday, a new student came to our class. His name was Carlos, and he came from Spain. At first, he was very shy and did not speak. Our teacher asked me to sit next to him. I said, "Hello, I am Fan. Do you like football?" His face lit up. "Yes! I love it!" he answered in slow English. At break, we played together, and he was much better than all of us. Soon, he made many friends. He taught us some Spanish words, and we taught him some Chinese. Now he says "ni hao" every morning with a big smile.

q.q: Where did Carlos come from?
Why did Carlos's face light up?
What does Carlos say every morning?

4.text: Our school started a recycling project this term. In every classroom, there are three bins: one for paper, one for plastic and one for other rubbish. At first, many children put things in the wrong bin, so we made colourful signs. Every Friday, a group of students counts the paper. Last month, we collected nearly two hundred kilograms! A truck took it to a factory, where workers turn old paper into new paper. One tonne of recycled paper saves about seventeen trees. Now we use both sides of every page, and we feel proud that we help the planet.

q.q: How many bins are in each classroom?
Why did the students make signs?
q.a: Many children used the wrong bin

q.q: What happens to the paper at the factory?

4.t: The Race to the South Pole
4.text: In 1911, two teams wanted to be the first to reach the South Pole, the coldest place on Earth. The Norwegian team, led by Roald Amundsen, used dogs to pull their sleds. The British team, led by Robert Scott, used ponies and men. The dogs were faster and stronger in the snow. Amundsen's team arrived on 14 December 1911, and then they went home safely. Scott's team came thirty-four days later and found a Norwegian flag there. Sadly, they did not return alive. Today, people remember both men as brave, but they say the dogs made the difference.

q.q: Who arrived at the South Pole first?
What did Amundsen's team use?
What did Scott's team find at the Pole?

4.text: Long ago, a poor farmer found an old clay pot in his field. He took it home, and by accident, he dropped a coin into it. Then there were two coins in the pot! He put in a bag of rice, and a moment later, there were two bags. The farmer was amazed. "This is a magic pot," he said. Soon he became rich, but a greedy neighbour wanted the pot. One night, the neighbour stole it. But he fell into the pot, and it made two neighbours. They argued so loudly that everyone in the village came running.
4.src: adapted from a Chinese folk tale (public domain)

q.q: What happened when the farmer dropped a coin into the pot?
Why did the neighbour take the pot?
What happened to the neighbour?

4.text: A plane is very heavy, but it can fly high in the sky. How is this possible? The secret is in the wings. They have a special shape. When the plane moves forward very fast, the air goes over and under the wings. The air above moves faster, and this makes a force that pushes the wings up. This force is called lift. The engines push the plane forward, and a big plane needs a very long runway to get enough speed. The pilot can change the angle of the wings to go up or down. Planes carry millions of people safely every day.

q.q: Where is the secret of flying?
What does a big plane need to get enough speed?
What is lift?
q.a: A force that pushes the wings up

4.text: Alice was sitting by the river with her sister. She was bored because the book had no pictures. Suddenly, a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran past her. It took a watch out of its pocket and said, "Oh dear! I shall be late!" Alice had never seen a rabbit with a watch, so she jumped up and ran after it. The rabbit went down a big hole under a hedge. Alice followed it and fell down, down, down. It seemed to be a very deep well. Alice wondered where she would end up.
4.src: adapted from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Lewis Carroll (public domain)

q.q: Why was Alice bored?
What was strange about the rabbit?
Where did the rabbit go?

4.text: In autumn, millions of people in India celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights. The festival lasts five days. Before it begins, families clean and paint their houses. They put small clay lamps called diyas in windows and doors, so there are thousands of tiny lights everywhere at night. People wear their best clothes and make colourful patterns on the floor with powder. They also share sweets with friends and neighbours. There are fireworks, too, and children love them. The festival teaches that light is stronger than darkness and that good always wins in the end.

q.q: How long does Diwali last?
What are diyas?
What does the festival teach?

4.text: Mr Lee built a small robot for his son Danny. It was not like a robot in films. It was only thirty centimetres tall and had two round eyes. At first, it could only say "Hello" and move forward. Danny was a little disappointed. But every week, they added a new part. Soon the robot could turn left and right, pick up a ball and tell the time. One evening, it even brought Danny's slippers to his bed! Danny laughed so much. Now he wants to be an engineer and build a robot that can help old people.

q.q: Who built the robot?
Why was Danny disappointed at first?
q.a: The robot could do very little

q.q: What does Danny want to be?

4.text: The Great Wall of China is one of the longest buildings in the world. Parts of it are more than two thousand years old. The first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, joined older walls together to keep enemies out. Later, other rulers made it longer and stronger. The Ming wall, which most visitors see today, is made of brick and stone. In some places, it is as high as a house and wide enough for five horses. There are towers on the wall where soldiers watched for danger and sent smoke signals. Millions of people visit the wall every year.

q.q: Why was the Great Wall built?
w: To show the beauty of China
To make a road for horses

q.q: What is the Ming wall made of?
What did soldiers do in the towers?

4.text: Last night, Nina woke up because she heard a strange noise from the kitchen. Scratch, scratch, crunch. She was a little afraid, but she took her torch and went downstairs very quietly.
