There was a light under the kitchen door! Slowly, she opened it. In the middle of the floor sat her cat, Pepper, and next to him was a small grey mouse. They were both eating a piece of cheese together! Nina could not believe her eyes. She laughed so loudly that the mouse ran away. Pepper looked at her as if nothing had happened.

q.q: Why did Nina go downstairs?
What was Pepper doing?
Why did the mouse run away?

4.text: Marie Curie was born in Poland in 1867. As a girl, she loved books and was the best student in her school. Her country was poor then, and women could not study at university there, so she moved to Paris when she was twenty-four. She worked very hard and often had only bread and tea for dinner. With her husband Pierre, she discovered two new elements, polonium and radium. In 1903, she won the Nobel Prize for physics, and in 1911, she won a second prize, for chemistry. She was the first person ever to win two Nobel Prizes, and she is still a hero for many young scientists.

q.q: Why did Marie move to Paris?
q.a: Women could not study at university in her country
w: She wanted to be a teacher

q.q: What did Marie and Pierre discover?
What was special about Marie's prizes?
q.a: She was the first to win two

4.text: One Saturday morning, Aunt Polly told Tom to paint the long white fence. Tom was very sad. All the other boys were free to play! He began to paint slowly. Then Ben, a friend, came by and laughed at him. Tom did not look up. "Work? I like painting," he said. "It is not every day that a boy gets to paint a fence." Ben wanted to try, and Tom let him, but only after Ben gave him an apple. Soon many boys came, and each paid something. By afternoon, the fence was white three times over, and Tom was rich with toys and apples.
4.src: adapted from The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, Mark Twain (public domain)

q.q: What did Aunt Polly tell Tom to do?
How did Tom get the other boys to paint?
What did Tom get from the boys?

4.text: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers, and their wings work like flippers. Most penguins live in the cold south, and the biggest one, the emperor penguin, lives in Antarctica. It is about one metre tall. In winter, the female lays one egg, and then she goes to the sea to eat. The father keeps the egg warm on his feet for two months, and he eats nothing at all. The penguins stand close together in a big group to stay warm. When the baby comes out, the mother comes back with food.

q.q: What do penguins use their wings for?
Who keeps the egg warm?
Why do penguins stand close together?

4.text: High above the city stood the statue of the Happy Prince. He was covered with gold, and his eyes were two bright blue stones. One night, a little swallow stopped to sleep at his feet. The prince was crying! "I can see all the sad things in the city," he said. "There is a poor woman with a sick child. Please take the red stone from my sword to her." The swallow did this. Night after night, he carried the prince's gold and jewels to the poor. The bird stayed too long, and the cold winter came. He died at the prince's feet, but he was happy.
4.src: adapted from The Happy Prince, Oscar Wilde (public domain)

q.q: What were the prince's eyes?
Why was the prince crying?
q.a: He saw sad things in the city

q.q: What happened to the swallow?
q.a: He stayed too long and died in winter

4.text: Beijing South is one of the busiest railway stations in China. Every day, about three hundred thousand passengers walk through its big halls. The roof is shaped like an oval and is much higher than a normal station roof. There are more than twenty platforms, and fast trains leave every few minutes. A trip from Beijing to Shanghai takes only about four and a half hours. In the past, it took more than ten hours. Travellers need to arrive early, find their gate and show their tickets. Many people say the station feels more like an airport than a train station.

q.q: How long does a trip from Beijing to Shanghai take today?
q.a: About four and a half hours

q.q: What shape is the roof?
What do many people say about the station?

4.text: It was the last evening of the year, and it was snowing hard. A poor little girl walked in the street with bare feet. She had a lot of matches in her old apron, but nobody bought any. She was cold and hungry, and she did not dare to go home, because her father would be angry. She sat in a corner and lit a match. In its warm light, she saw a big stove. Then the match went out, and the stove was gone. She lit another match and saw a table full of food. At last, she saw her kind grandmother, who took her in her arms.
4.src: adapted from The Little Match Girl, Hans Christian Andersen (public domain)

q.q: What did the girl sell?
Why did she not go home?
Who did she see at last?

4.text: Only a small part of the water on Earth is fresh water that we can drink, and in many places, there is not enough of it. In the past, people in cities used water without thinking. Now we know that we must save it. Here are some simple ways. Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Take a short shower instead of a long bath. Use a bucket to wash the car, and use the water from washing rice for the plants. A tap that drips can waste more than ten thousand litres in a year. If everybody helps a little, we can save a lot.

q.q: How can we save water when brushing teeth?
What can a dripping tap do?
q.a: Waste thousands of litres a year

q.q: What is the main idea?

4.t: A Letter to My Pen Friend
4.text: Dear Sophie, Thank you for your letter and your photo. You look very friendly! I live in Shanghai, which is a very big city. There are more than twenty million people here, and the buildings are taller than any I have seen in photos of your town. My school is only ten minutes from my home, and I walk there with my friends. At the weekend, I play badminton and learn English online. In winter, we sometimes eat hot pot with the whole family. What do you do after school? Please write soon and tell me about your country. Best wishes, Mei

q.q: Where does Mei live?
How does Mei go to school?
What does Mei ask Sophie?

4.text: In winter, many people love to play in the snow. Skiing is a popular sport, and you can find it in the mountains of northern China, Japan and Europe. Skiers wear special boots and slide down hills on two long boards. Skating is another favourite. On a frozen lake or in an ice rink, skaters glide, turn and even jump. In 2022, Beijing hosted the Winter Olympics, the first city to host both the summer and winter games. Chinese athletes won nine gold medals, and many children began to try ice sports after watching them. Remember to wear a helmet and warm clothes.

q.q: What do skiers slide on?
What was special about Beijing?
q.a: It hosted both summer and winter Olympics

q.q: Why did many children try ice sports?

4.text: It was Christmas Eve, and Jim and Della were poor. Each of them wanted to buy a present for the other, but they had almost no money. Della loved Jim's gold watch, but it had no chain. Jim loved Della's long, beautiful hair, and she wanted combs for it. So Della sold her hair and bought a chain for the watch. When Jim came home, he stopped and stared. He had sold his watch to buy her the combs! They looked at each other and began to laugh. "We are both silly," said Della. But they knew that their love was the best gift of all.
4.src: adapted from The Gift of the Magi, O. Henry (public domain)

q.q: What did Della sell?
What did Jim sell?
What is the main idea?

4.text: Soon the year will end, and I like to look back. In January, I was only nine, and I could not swim. In summer, my uncle taught me, and now I can swim two lengths of the pool. I read twenty-five books this year, and my favourite was a story about a clever fox. At school, I made new friends and learned to play the flute. There were hard days, too. I failed a maths test in March, but I studied harder and passed the next one. Next year, I want to learn to cook, visit the sea again and help my little sister with her English.

q.q: Who taught the writer to swim?
What happened in March?
What does the writer want to do next year?

5.text: It is the first week of January. Tom sits at his desk with a pen and a piece of paper. He is making a plan for the new year. 'I am going to read one book every month,' he writes. 'I will also practise the piano for twenty minutes every day.' Then he stops and thinks. Last year he made a big plan, but he forgot it after two weeks. This year he wants to be different. So he writes a small plan and puts it on the wall beside his bed. Every evening he will look at it and tick the things he did. Tom smiles. 'Small steps are better than big dreams,' he says. 'And I will start tomorrow morning!'

q.q: What is Tom going to read?
Why does Tom write a small plan this year?
q.a: His big plan last year did not work
w: He has no time to read
He does not like the piano

q.q: What does the word 'tick' mean in the text?
q.a: Make a mark to show something is done

5.text: One day a crow found a big piece of cheese. She flew up to a high branch of a tree and sat there happily. A hungry fox saw her from below. He wanted the cheese, but he could not climb the tree. So he thought of a clever plan. 'Good morning, beautiful crow!' he said. 'Your feathers are so black and shiny. I am sure your voice is also lovely. Will you sing a song for me?' The crow felt very proud. She opened her mouth to sing, and the cheese fell down. The fox caught it and ran away. 'Thank you for the lunch,' he laughed. The crow learned a lesson that day: do not believe every sweet word.
5.src: adapted from The Fox and the Crow, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why could the fox not get the cheese himself?
q.a: He could not climb the tree
w: He was afraid of the crow

q.q: What is the main idea of the story?
q.a: Do not believe every sweet word

q.q: What did the fox say about the crow's feathers?

5.text: Mia and her father are going to visit her grandmother in Shanghai. They get on the train at nine o'clock in the morning. Mia has a seat by the window, and she watches the fields, rivers and small villages pass by. The train is very fast. After two hours, she eats a sandwich and drinks some juice. Then she plays a card game with her father. A kind woman across the aisle gives her an apple. Mia says thank you and shares her biscuits with the woman. In the afternoon the train arrives at the big station. Grandmother is waiting on the platform with a happy smile. Mia runs to hug her.

q.q: Who is Mia going to visit?
What does Mia do after eating?
Where is Grandmother waiting?

5.text: Many birds fly to warmer places in autumn. We call this journey migration. In winter the weather in the north is very cold, and there is little food. Insects hide and the lakes freeze. So the birds go south, where it is warm and they can find plenty to eat. Some birds fly thousands of kilometres. The wild goose often flies in the shape of a letter V. The bird at the front works hardest, and the others follow behind. After some time, they change places, so nobody gets too tired. In spring the birds will come back to the north and build new nests. Scientists use small tags to learn where the birds travel.

q.q: Why do birds fly south in autumn?
q.a: It is warmer and there is more food
w: They want to meet new friends
The north has too many people
They like to see the sea

q.q: Why do wild geese change places?
What will the birds do in spring?
q.a: Come back and build new nests

5.text: On the last evening of the old year, Lin's family has a big dinner. Everyone comes to Grandpa's house: aunts, uncles and cousins. In the kitchen, Grandma and Mum make a lot of dumplings. Lin helps them, but her dumplings look very strange. 'They look like little boats!' laughs her cousin. After dinner, the children get red envelopes with some money inside. Then the family watches the festival show on television. At midnight, people outside begin to set off fireworks. The sky becomes bright with red, gold and green lights. Lin covers her ears and smiles. She is happy because the whole family is together. Tomorrow she will visit her friends and wish them a good year.

q.q: What do Grandma and Mum make?
Why does Lin feel happy at the end?
What will Lin do tomorrow?

5.text: My uncle Ben is a pilot. He flies big planes from China to many countries in Europe and Asia. He wears a smart blue uniform and a white hat. Uncle Ben loves his job, but it is not always easy. He must wake up very early, and sometimes he is away from home for many days. Before every flight he checks the weather and the plane carefully. 'Safety is the most important thing,' he says. Last month he flew to Paris, and he brought me a small model of the Eiffel Tower. When I am older, I want to be a pilot too. First, I must study hard, learn English well and keep my eyes healthy.

q.q: What does Uncle Ben do before every flight?
q.a: He checks the weather and the plane

q.q: What did Uncle Ben bring from Paris?
q.a: A small model of the Eiffel Tower

q.q: What is hard about his job?
q.a: He is often away from home
w: He has no holidays at all

5.text: A hare was very proud of his speed. One day he laughed at a slow tortoise. 'You walk so slowly!' he said. 'Let us have a race, and I will win easily.' The tortoise agreed. All the animals came to watch. At the start, the hare ran far ahead. He looked back and saw that the tortoise was only a small point on the road. 'I have plenty of time,' he thought, and he lay down under a tree for a rest. Soon he was fast asleep. The tortoise did not stop. He walked step by step, and he never gave up. When the hare woke up, the tortoise was already near the finish line. The hare ran as fast as he could, but it was too late.
5.src: adapted from The Tortoise and the Hare, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why did the hare lie down?
q.a: He thought he had plenty of time
w: He wanted to help the tortoise

q.q: What is the main idea of the story?
What did the tortoise do during the race?
q.a: He kept walking and never gave up
w: He ran past the hare at the start

5.text: Anna is shopping with her mother at a big market. There are many people, and Anna sees a stall with colourful toys. She stops to look. When she turns around, her mother is gone! Anna feels afraid, but she remembers her mother's advice: 'Stay where you are, and ask a helper.' She sees a woman in a green uniform. 'Excuse me,' Anna says, 'I am lost. I cannot find my mum.' The woman smiles. 'Do not worry. What is your mother's name?' She speaks into a small microphone, and her voice comes out of loud speakers. Two minutes later, Anna's mother runs to her and holds her tightly. 'I am so sorry,' says Anna. 'Next time, I will hold your hand.'

q.q: Why does Anna stop?
q.a: She wants to look at some toys

q.q: What does Anna do when she is lost?
q.a: She asks a helper for help
w: She runs out of the market
She cries and sits on the floor

q.q: What will Anna do next time?

5.text: Water never goes away. It travels around the Earth again and again. We call this the water cycle. First, the sun warms the sea, the rivers and the lakes. Some of the water becomes a gas called vapour and rises into the air. High in the sky it is cold, so the vapour turns into tiny drops of water. These drops make clouds. When the clouds become heavy, the water falls back to the ground as rain or snow. Then it runs into streams and rivers, and flows to the sea. After that, the sun warms the water again, and the journey starts once more. The water you drink today may be millions of years old!

q.q: What warms the water first?
How do clouds form?
q.a: Vapour turns into tiny drops of water

q.q: What is the main idea of the text?
q.a: Water travels around the Earth again and again

5.text: Marie Curie was born in Poland in 1867. Her family was not rich, but she loved to learn. At that time, girls could not go to university in her country, so she moved to Paris when she was twenty-four. She studied science and worked very hard. In Paris she met a young scientist called Pierre, and they got married. Together they discovered two new elements, and Marie gave one of them the name polonium after her home country. She won two Nobel Prizes, one in physics and one in chemistry. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. During the First World War, she also helped doctors with special machines that could take pictures inside the body. Marie Curie is still a hero for many girls who love science.

q.q: Why did Marie move to Paris?
q.a: Girls could not go to university in Poland
w: She wanted to be an actress

q.q: Where does the name polonium come from?
What did Marie Curie do in the war?
q.a: She helped doctors with special machines

5.t: A Football Match in the Rain
5.text: On Saturday our school team played a football match against Green Hill School. In the morning the sun was shining, but at two o'clock the sky turned dark and it started to rain heavily. The field became wet and muddy. Some players slipped and fell down, and everybody was laughing. At half time we were losing by one goal. 'Do not give up,' said our coach. 'Pass the ball quickly and stay together.' In the second half, Jack kicked the ball into the net, and the score was one all. Then, two minutes before the end, Lucy scored an amazing goal! We won two to one. We were cold and dirty, but we were very happy. After the match, we drank hot chocolate and went home.

q.q: What was the weather at two o'clock?
Who scored the winning goal?
What does the word 'amazing' mean here?

5.text: The Great Wall of China is one of the most famous buildings in the world. People built it over many hundreds of years. Different kings added new parts to protect their land from enemies. The wall goes over high mountains and across dry deserts. Along the wall there are towers. Soldiers used them to watch for danger. When enemies came, the soldiers made smoke or fire on top of a tower, and the next tower did the same. In this way, the news travelled very fast. Today, the wall is quiet, and visitors from all over the world come to walk on it. Many people say it is hard to climb, but the view from the top is wonderful. If you visit it in autumn, you will see beautiful red leaves.

q.q: Why did kings build parts of the wall?
q.a: To protect their land from enemies
w: To make a road for cars
To keep animals out of the farms

q.q: How did soldiers send news?
q.a: With smoke or fire on the towers

q.q: What will you see in autumn?

5.text: Last week Sam ate too many sweets. On Friday night he had a terrible pain in his tooth. He could not sleep, and he did not want any breakfast the next morning. 'You must see a dentist,' said his mother. At the dentist's office, Sam felt nervous. Dr Wang was a friendly woman. She looked inside his mouth with a small mirror. 'You have a hole in one tooth,' she said. 'But do not worry. I will fix it, and it will not hurt very much.' After half an hour, the pain was gone. Dr Wang gave Sam some advice: 'Brush your teeth twice a day, eat fewer sweets and drink more water.' Sam nodded. From now on, he is going to take good care of his teeth.

q.q: Why did Sam have a pain in his tooth?
w: He did not wash his hands

q.q: What did Dr Wang say about the hole?
w: It was too big to fix
Sam must stay at the hospital

q.q: What is Sam going to do from now on?
q.a: Take good care of his teeth

5.text: A lion was sleeping in the forest when a little mouse ran across his nose. The lion woke up and caught the mouse in his big paw. 'Please let me go,' said the mouse. 'One day I will help you.' The lion laughed. 'How can a tiny mouse help a king?' But he let the mouse go. A few days later, hunters caught the lion in a strong net. He roared loudly, but he could not escape. The mouse heard him and ran quickly to the place. She bit the ropes again and again with her sharp teeth. At last the net broke, and the lion was free. 'Now you see,' said the mouse, 'even a small friend can be a great help.'
5.src: adapted from The Lion and the Mouse, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why did the lion let the mouse go?
q.a: The mouse said she would help him one day

q.q: How did the mouse free the lion?
q.a: She bit the ropes of the net
w: She pulled him with her paws

q.q: What is the lesson of the story?
q.a: Small friends can give great help

5.text: Last Sunday my family went to the beach. We got up at six o'clock and drove for two hours. The sea was blue and calm, but the water was still a bit cold. My little brother wanted to swim at once, but Dad said, 'First, we must put on sun cream.' Then we built a big sandcastle with towers and a deep hole around it. My sister found some pretty shells and put them on the top. At noon we had a picnic under a big umbrella. Suddenly a seagull flew down and took a sandwich from Dad's hand! Everybody laughed, and Dad said, 'Next time, I will eat inside the car.' We came home tired, brown and very happy.

q.q: What did Dad say they must do first?
What happened at the picnic?
How did the family feel at the end of the day?

5.text: Bees are small but very busy animals. In spring and summer, worker bees fly from flower to flower. They drink a sweet liquid called nectar and carry it home in their bodies. At the hive, they give the nectar to other bees. These bees chew it and then put it into little wax rooms. Then they move their wings very fast to dry the liquid. After a few days, it becomes thick and sweet. This is honey! Bees keep the honey as food for winter, when there are no flowers. Bees also help us in another way. When they move from flower to flower, they carry pollen, and this helps plants make fruit. Without bees, we would have much less food to eat.

q.q: What do worker bees collect from flowers?
Why do bees keep honey?
How do bees help plants?
q.a: They carry pollen from flower to flower

5.text: In April the weather gets warmer and the wind is soft and steady. It is the perfect time to fly a kite. This year Yuki and her grandfather are going to make a kite together. Grandfather cuts thin bamboo sticks and ties them into a frame. Yuki covers the frame with light paper and paints a big orange butterfly on it. Then they tie a long string to the kite and add a tail made of colourful cloth. On Saturday they walk to the park. At first the kite will not fly, and it falls on the grass twice. Then a good wind comes. Yuki runs, lets out more string, and the butterfly rises high into the blue sky. 'It is flying!' she shouts happily.

q.q: What does Yuki paint on the kite?
Why does the kite fall at first?
What does Grandfather use to make the frame?

5.text: A young shepherd boy looked after the village sheep on a hill. The days were long and he was bored. One afternoon he thought of a game. 'Wolf! Wolf!' he shouted. 'A wolf is eating the sheep!' The villagers ran up the hill with sticks, but they found no wolf. The boy laughed at them. A few days later he played the same trick again, and again the villagers came. They were angry. Then one evening a real wolf came out of the forest. The boy cried, 'Wolf! Wolf! Please help me!' But nobody came, because the villagers thought it was another joke. That night the boy lost many sheep. He learned that people do not believe a liar, even when he tells the truth.
5.src: adapted from The Boy Who Cried Wolf, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: Why did the boy shout 'Wolf'?
q.a: He was bored and wanted a game

q.q: Why did nobody come the last time?
q.a: They thought it was another joke

q.q: What is the lesson of the story?

5.text: Last spring our class started a small garden behind the school. Our teacher, Mr Lee, gave each group a piece of land. First, we dug the soil and took out the stones. Then we planted tomatoes, carrots and beans. Every morning two students gave water to the plants. In May, the beans began to climb up their sticks, and we were all very excited. But one day we found small holes in the leaves. 'Insects!' said Mr Lee. We did not want to use strong chemicals, so we picked the insects off by hand. In June we picked our first tomatoes and ate them with bread at lunch. They tasted better than any tomato from the shop. Next year, we are going to grow pumpkins and sunflowers too.

q.q: What did the students plant first?
How did they deal with the insects?
q.a: They picked them off by hand

q.q: What will they grow next year?

5.text: Mr Chen is a children's doctor at a hospital in our town. Every morning he arrives at the hospital at seven thirty and checks his first patients. Many children are afraid of doctors, so he tells jokes and shows them funny pictures. 'A smile is the best medicine,' he often says. He listens to their hearts with a stethoscope and looks into their throats with a small light. When a child has a cold, he tells the family to rest and drink water. When the problem is more serious, he sends the child for tests. Mr Chen works long hours, and sometimes he even works at night. 'I am tired,' he says, 'but I feel proud when a child gets well and goes home.' His job is hard, but it is also a very kind job.

q.q: Why does Mr Chen tell jokes?
q.a: Many children are afraid of doctors
w: He wants to be an actor

q.q: What does he do for a child with a cold?
q.a: Tells the family to rest and drink water

q.q: What makes Mr Chen proud?
q.a: A child gets well and goes home
w: He gets a lot of money

5.text: Giant pandas live in the mountains of Sichuan, in the south-west of China. They love bamboo forests, because bamboo is their main food. An adult panda eats for about twelve hours a day, and it can eat more than ten kilograms of bamboo. This is because bamboo does not give much energy. When a baby panda is born, it is very small, pink and blind. It is only about as big as a cup of tea! The mother takes good care of it for many months. Pandas were in danger for many years, because people cut down forests. Now China has special reserves, and the number of wild pandas is growing again. Many people travel to Chengdu every year to see these gentle, black and white animals.

q.q: Why does a panda eat so much bamboo?
q.a: Bamboo does not give much energy

q.q: What was the danger for pandas?
What is true about a new baby panda?
q.a: It is very small and cannot see

5.text: The Dragon Boat Festival is on the fifth day of the fifth month of the Chinese calendar. Many years ago, there was a poet called Qu Yuan. He loved his country very much, but he was very sad when the king did not listen to him. In the end he jumped into a river. The local people were sad too. They quickly rowed their boats on the river to look for him, and they threw rice into the water so the fish would not eat his body. Today people remember him in the same way. They race in long boats that have a dragon's head, and everybody beats a big drum to keep the rowers together. Families also eat zongzi, which is sticky rice wrapped in leaves. My favourite one has sweet red beans inside.

q.q: Why were people sad about Qu Yuan?
w: He left the country by train

q.q: Why does the drummer beat the drum?
What is zongzi?

5.text: Ben could not swim, and he was afraid of deep water. When his class went to the swimming pool, he stayed in the shallow end and held the wall. His teacher, Ms Ma, came to him and said, 'Everybody is afraid of something. Let us start slowly.' First, she showed him how to blow bubbles in the water. Then she taught him how to float on his back. 'Relax your body, and the water will carry you,' she said. After four lessons, Ben could move his arms and legs together. On the last day, he swam across the pool without any help! His friends clapped and shouted, 'Well done!' Ben was very proud of himself. Next summer, he is going to join the school swimming team.

q.q: Where did Ben stay at first?
What did Ms Ma teach him first?
q.a: To blow bubbles in the water

q.q: What will Ben do next summer?

5.text: Thomas Edison was an American inventor who lived about one hundred and fifty years ago. As a boy he was very curious. He asked a lot of questions, and his teacher thought he was slow. So his mother taught him at home. She told him that he was very clever. Later, Edison built a laboratory and worked there day and night with his helpers. He made the first useful light bulb that could burn for a long time. To find the right material for it, he tried thousands of different things, and most of them did not work. 'I have not failed,' he said. 'I have just found many ways that will not work.' Edison also invented a machine that could record sound. Today we still use many of his ideas.

q.q: Who taught Edison at home?
What did Edison say about his failures?
q.a: He found many ways that do not work

q.q: What does 'curious' mean here?

5.text: All summer a grasshopper sang and danced in the sun. 'Life is wonderful!' he said. Nearby, a group of ants worked very hard. They carried grains of corn and rice to their nest, and the pile of food became bigger every day. 'Why do you work so much?' asked the grasshopper. 'Come and play with me!' 'We are preparing for winter,' said one ant. 'You should do the same.' The grasshopper only laughed. When winter came, there was snow everywhere, and he could not find any food. He was cold and hungry. At last he knocked on the ants' door. 'Please give me something to eat,' he said. The ants were kind, and they shared some food with him, but he never forgot that winter. The next summer he worked too.
5.src: adapted from The Ant and the Grasshopper, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: What did the ants do in summer?
Why was the grasshopper hungry in winter?
q.a: He had not saved any food

q.q: What did the ants do at the end?
q.a: They shared some food with him

5.text: In Ella's house there is a new rule: no phones at the dinner table. Her father started it last month. 'We never talk to each other any more,' he said. 'Everyone looks at a screen.' At first Ella was unhappy, because she wanted to chat with her friends during dinner. But after a week, she changed her mind. Now the family talks about school, work and funny things that happened that day. Ella also has a rule for herself: she plays games on her tablet for one hour only, and she stops two hours before bed. 'When I look at a screen late at night, I sleep badly,' she says. On Sundays her family goes for a walk without any phones. 'The real world is much more interesting than a small screen,' Ella says.

q.q: Why did Ella's father make the new rule?
q.a: The family did not talk to each other
w: He wanted to buy a new table

q.q: What does Ella do before bed?
q.a: She stops using screens two hours before
w: She plays games for an hour

q.q: What does 'changed her mind' mean?

5.text: In July Leo went to a summer camp in the mountains for one week. He shared a tent with three boys, and on the first night they could not sleep because the forest was full of strange sounds. In the morning a guide taught them how to read a map and how to use a compass. In the afternoon they climbed a hill, and Leo was surprised that he did not get tired. At night everybody sat round the campfire. They sang songs, told stories and watched the stars, which were much brighter than in the city. On the last day it rained, but nobody was sad. They played games in the big tent and ate hot soup. 'I will come again next year,' Leo told his new friends, 'and I am going to bring my own guitar.'

q.q: Why could the boys not sleep on the first night?
q.a: The forest was full of strange sounds

q.q: What did Leo see at night that was different from the city?
What is Leo going to do next year?
q.a: Come again and bring a guitar

5.text: The moon is Earth's closest neighbour in space. It is about four hundred thousand kilometres away from us, and it takes about a month to travel once around our planet. The moon does not make its own light. It looks bright because it reflects the light of the sun. The moon seems to change its shape from night to night, but it is always round. We only see the part that the sun is shining on. When we see all of it, we call it a full moon. There is no air or water on the moon, so nothing can live there. In 1969, two American astronauts walked on its dusty surface for the first time. They left their footprints, and because there is no wind, the prints are probably still there today.

q.q: Why does the moon look bright?
q.a: It reflects the light of the sun
w: It is very close to us

q.q: Why are the footprints probably still there?
q.a: There is no wind on the moon

q.q: What is a full moon?
q.a: When we can see all of the sunlit part
w: When the moon is very far
When it is a very small moon

5.t: A Funny Mistake at the Restaurant
5.text: Last Friday my uncle took me to a new restaurant. It had a long menu with pictures. My uncle wanted a bowl of noodles, and he asked the waiter, 'Could I have the noodles with beef, please?' The waiter nodded and went away. Ten minutes later he came back with a big plate of rice and fish. 'I am sorry,' my uncle said, 'but this is not what I asked for.' The waiter looked at his paper and went red. 'Oh no!' he said. 'I gave your order to the family at table five, and they got your noodles.' We laughed, and the waiter laughed too. Soon the right food arrived, and the manager brought us a free dessert. It was a big bowl of ice cream, and it tasted much better than the noodles!

q.q: What did the uncle want to eat?
What was the waiter's mistake?
q.a: He gave the order to another table

q.q: What did the manager give them?
w: A free dinner for a week

5.text: Next month Hana's family is going to fly to London. It will be her first trip to another country, and she is very excited. She has read about the city in books, and she has made a list of places to visit. First, she wants to see Big Ben, the famous clock tower. Then they will take a boat on the River Thames and look at the old bridges. Hana's father wants to visit the museums, because many of them are free. Her mother loves shopping, so they will walk down busy streets full of shops. Hana is also learning some English phrases. 'Excuse me, where is the station?' she practises every evening. She is a little nervous about the long flight, but she will bring a good book and a pillow for the plane.

q.q: What does Hana want to see first?
Why does her father like the museums?
How does Hana feel about the long flight?

5.t: The Goose with the Golden Eggs
5.text: Long ago a poor farmer had a very special goose. Every morning she laid an egg, and the egg was made of pure gold! The farmer sold the eggs in the town and soon he became rich. But he was not happy for long. He wanted more, and he did not like to wait for one egg every day. 'The goose must have a lot of gold inside her,' he thought. 'If I cut her open, I can have it all at once!' So he took a knife and killed the goose. But inside there was only a normal goose, with no gold at all. The farmer cried and cried, but it was too late. He had lost his wonderful goose, and there would be no more golden eggs. He was poor again, because he was greedy.
5.src: adapted from The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: What was special about the goose?
q.a: She laid a golden egg every morning

q.q: Why did the farmer kill the goose?
q.a: He wanted all the gold at once

q.q: What is the lesson of the story?
q.a: Being greedy can make you lose everything

5.text: Kevin is twelve years old, and he wants to be a chef. At weekends he helps his grandfather in the kitchen of the family restaurant. First he washes the vegetables and cuts them into small pieces. 'Be careful with the knife,' says his grandfather. 'A good chef is always safe and clean.' Last Sunday Kevin cooked his first real dish: egg fried rice. He heated the oil, added the eggs, and then the cold rice. But he used too much salt, and the customers made funny faces when they tasted it. Kevin felt embarrassed, but his grandfather only smiled. 'Even famous chefs make mistakes,' he said. 'You will do better next time.' This week Kevin is going to try again, and he will taste the food before he serves it.

q.q: What does Kevin do first when he helps in the kitchen?
What was wrong with Kevin's fried rice?
What will Kevin do this week?
q.a: Try again and taste the food first

5.text: A rain forest is a thick forest in a warm place where it rains almost every day. The biggest rain forest in the world is in South America, along the Amazon River. It is home to millions of different kinds of animals and plants. Colourful parrots fly between the tall trees, monkeys jump from branch to branch, and snakes hide under the leaves. The trees grow so close together that very little sunlight reaches the ground. The trees give us a lot of the oxygen we breathe. Sadly, people are cutting down large areas of rain forest to make farms and roads. When the trees disappear, many animals lose their homes. If we use less paper and buy wood from protected forests, we can help save this precious part of our planet.

q.q: Where is the biggest rain forest?
Why does very little sunlight reach the ground?
How can we help the rain forests?
q.a: Use less paper and buy protected wood
w: Plant trees in the desert only

5.text: Table tennis is called the national sport of China, and many children begin to play when they are very young. Lily started at the age of six. Her father put a small table in the living room, and they played together every evening. At eight she joined a club, where a coach taught her how to hold the bat and how to spin the ball. She trained for two hours after school, five days a week. Sometimes she lost matches and cried, but her coach said, 'Every loss teaches you something.' Last year Lily won the city championship for children under twelve. Her prize was a small gold cup, and she put it next to her bed. Now she dreams of playing for the national team. 'I will keep training,' she says, 'and I will never stop learning.'

q.q: Where did Lily play with her father?
What did her coach say about losing?
What is Lily's dream?
q.a: To play for the national team

5.text: Robots are machines that can do jobs for people. Many factories use robots to build cars. A robot arm can lift heavy parts, and it never gets tired. Some robots work in hospitals and help doctors carry out difficult operations. Others clean our floors at home, and some even bring food to the tables in restaurants. Robots are very good at doing the same thing again and again, but they cannot think like us, and they do not understand feelings. Some people worry that robots will take their jobs. Experts say that new kinds of work will also appear, such as designing, repairing and teaching robots. If you enjoy mathematics and science, you could start learning to write computer programs now, because every robot needs a clever program to tell it what to do.

q.q: What are robots very good at?
q.a: Doing the same thing again and again

q.q: What do experts say about new jobs?
q.a: New kinds of work will appear

q.q: What does every robot need?

5.text: More than two thousand years ago, traders began to travel along a long road from China to the countries in the west. We call it the Silk Road, because the most famous thing they carried was silk, a soft cloth that people in Europe loved. The journey was not easy. The traders crossed high mountains and hot deserts, and it could take them many months. They travelled in groups called caravans, with camels that carried heavy bags. Nobody usually went the whole way. Traders sold their goods to others at markets on the way. Besides silk, they also exchanged tea, spices, paper and glass. Along with goods, ideas moved too: people shared religions, music, stories and inventions. Today China is building new roads and railways to connect the world again, and many call this project a new Silk Road.

q.q: Why is it called the Silk Road?
q.a: Silk was the most famous thing carried
w: It was built by silk makers
It went through a silk factory

q.q: How did traders usually travel?
What else moved along the road besides goods?

5.text: 'Hi, Jane! How were your holidays?' asked Alex on the first day of the new term. 'They were great,' said Jane. 'I went to my grandmother's farm, and I learned to ride a horse. What about you?' 'I stayed at home most of the time,' said Alex, 'but I read ten books and I learned to play chess.' 'That is wonderful! Do you know who our new teacher is?' 'Yes, I do. She is Miss Zhou, and she comes from Beijing. People say she is strict, but she is also very funny.' 'Good,' said Jane. The bell rang, and the two friends hurried into the classroom. 'Let us sit near the window,' said Alex. 'Then we can watch the birds when the lesson is boring.' Jane laughed. 'No, we will sit at the front, and we will listen carefully!'

q.q: What did Jane learn in the holidays?
What do people say about Miss Zhou?
Where do they decide to sit at the end?

5.text: The Mid-Autumn Festival is on the fifteenth day of the eighth month of the Chinese calendar. On this night the moon is round and bright, and it is a time for families to be together. People eat mooncakes, which are round, sweet cakes with different fillings inside, like red bean paste, lotus seeds or nuts. Long ago, a woman called Chang'e drank a magic medicine and flew up to the moon, where she lives with a white rabbit. Every year children look at the moon and try to find the rabbit on it. In our family, we sit in the garden and eat cakes. My grandfather says that the moon is the same everywhere, so when we look up, we are close to the people we love, even when they are far away.

q.q: When is the Mid-Autumn Festival?
q.a: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month
w: On the first day of the year
On the fifth day of the fifth month

q.q: Who lives on the moon in the story?
What does Grandfather say about the moon?
w: It is far from our garden
It is only round in China

5.t: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
5.text: A country mouse once invited his cousin from the town to dinner. The country mouse lived in a quiet field, and he served simple food: barley, beans and some cool water. The town mouse did not like it. 'Your life is too plain,' he said. 'Come to my house in the city. You will see how good life can be.' That evening they went to a big house. On the table there was cake, cheese, fruit and many other nice things. But just as they began to eat, the door opened with a bang, and a big cat jumped into the room. The mice ran away in fear. 'Thank you,' said the country mouse, when he was safe. 'But I prefer my simple dinner in peace to rich food with danger.' And he went home to his quiet field.
5.src: adapted from The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: What food did the country mouse serve?
What happened in the big house?
q.a: A cat jumped into the room

q.q: What does the country mouse prefer?
w: A rich life in the city

5.text: Mrs Wu packs a lunch box for her son Daniel every morning. She knows that a good lunch gives him energy for lessons and sports. Today the box has rice, a little chicken and some green vegetables. There is also an apple and a small bottle of water. Daniel does not like cabbage, but he eats it because his mother says it is good for his body. His friend Paul often brings crisps and a fizzy drink, and by two o'clock he feels sleepy in class. 'Sugar gives you quick energy, but then you feel tired again,' says their teacher. Daniel shares some of his apple with Paul. Next week Paul is going to bring a healthier lunch, and he will ask his mother to try Daniel's favourite recipe.

q.q: Why does Daniel eat cabbage?
q.a: His mother says it is good for his body
w: His teacher gave it to him

q.q: Why does Paul feel sleepy at two o'clock?
What will Paul do next week?

5.text: Water covers most of our planet, but only a tiny part of it is fresh water that we can drink. In some countries, people must walk many kilometres to get clean water, so we should not waste it. There are simple ways to save water at home. You can turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. A short shower uses much less water than a bath. If a tap drips, tell an adult to fix it, because a small drip can waste hundreds of litres in a year. You can also use the water from washing vegetables to give water to your plants. At school, our class made a poster with these ideas and put it on the wall of the toilets. Now many students remember to turn off the tap, and our school bill is lower.

q.q: How much of Earth's water can we drink?
What is a good way to save water?
q.a: Turn off the tap while brushing teeth

q.q: What happened after the class made a poster?
q.a: Many students remembered to turn off the tap

5.text: Louis Braille was born in France more than two hundred years ago. When he was three, he hurt his eye with a tool in his father's workshop, and soon he could not see at all. At that time, blind people had hardly any books. Louis went to a special school in Paris, where the students felt big raised letters with their fingers, but reading this way was very slow. Louis was a clever boy, and he wanted something better. When he was fifteen, he invented a new system with small raised dots, six in a box. Different groups of dots meant different letters. Blind people could read much faster with it. At first the school did not accept it, but after Louis died, braille spread all over the world. It is still used today.

q.q: How did Louis lose his sight?
q.a: He hurt his eye with a tool
w: He was ill for a year

q.q: What is braille made of?
What happened to braille after Louis died?
q.a: It spread all over the world

5.text: Wang Ming loves his bike. Last summer he made a plan to ride from his village to his aunt's town, forty kilometres away. His father agreed, but only if his cousin went with him. They left at seven o'clock with water, fruit and a map. The first part of the road was flat, and they rode fast. Then they came to a long hill, and they had to push their bikes. At noon they stopped under a tree and ate their lunch. Suddenly Wang Ming's tyre went flat! Luckily, an old man with a farm cart stopped and lent them a pump. They were late, but they arrived before dark. Aunt Li was waiting at the gate with a big bowl of hot noodles. 'You are brave boys,' she said, and they were too tired to answer.

q.q: Who went with Wang Ming on the trip?
How did the old man help?
How did the boys feel at the end?

5.text: One day the wind and the sun had an argument. Each of them said, 'I am stronger than you!' Then they saw a man walking along a road in a thick coat. 'Let us try,' said the sun. 'Whoever can make that man take off his coat is the stronger one.' The wind agreed and began first. He blew with all his strength, but the harder he blew, the tighter the man held his coat around him. At last the wind was tired and gave up. Then the sun began to shine, warm and soft. The man felt hot, and soon he took off his coat and sat down in the shade of a tree. The wind had to say that the sun was stronger. Kindness often works better than force.
5.src: adapted from The North Wind and the Sun, Aesop (public domain)

q.q: What did they want to see?
q.a: Who could make the man take off his coat
w: Who could blow a tree down

q.q: What did the man do when the wind blew hard?
What is the lesson of the story?
q.a: Kindness often works better than force

5.text: A volcano is a mountain with a hole at the top. Deep under the ground, the rock is so hot that it melts. This liquid rock is called magma. When there is too much pressure, the magma pushes up through the hole, and the volcano erupts. Once it comes out of the volcano, we call it lava. Lava can be red, orange and as hot as one thousand degrees. A big eruption also throws ash and gas high into the sky. This can be dangerous for villages near the mountain, so scientists watch active volcanoes carefully and warn people when they must leave. After many years, however, the cooled lava turns into rich soil, and farmers can grow good crops. Some of the most famous volcanoes are Mount Fuji in Japan and Vesuvius in Italy.

q.q: What is magma?
Why do scientists watch volcanoes?
q.a: To warn people when they must leave

q.q: How can lava help farmers?
q.a: It becomes rich soil after many years

5.text: Yao Ming was born in Shanghai in 1980. His parents were both basketball players, so it is not surprising that he became tall. By the age of fourteen he was already more than two metres tall. He started playing for a Shanghai team as a teenager,. In 2002 he went to America to play for the Houston Rockets. At first the game was very fast and physical for him, and the language was a problem, too. But he worked hard, learned English and became one of the best centres in the league. Fans loved him not only for his skill but also for his humour and kindness. After he stopped playing, he gave money to build schools and helped to protect wild animals.

q.q: Why was it not surprising that Yao Ming was tall?
w: He ate a lot of rice

q.q: What was difficult for him in America?
q.a: The fast game and the language

q.q: What did he do after he stopped playing?
q.a: He helped build schools and protect animals

5.text: Every night at midnight, a strange noise came from the garden of Mr Zhang. 'Miaow! Miaow!' It was so loud that he could not sleep. He was tired and angry, and he decided to find out what it was. One night he put on his coat, took a torch and went outside. Under the apple tree there was a small grey cat, and it was looking up into the branches. A tiny kitten was sitting there and was too afraid to come down! Mr Zhang laughed at himself. He got a ladder, climbed up and took the kitten in his arms. The mother cat jumped up and licked his hand. After that night, the cats came to visit him every evening. Now Mr Zhang sleeps well, and he buys fish for his new friends.

q.q: What made the noise?
q.a: A mother cat calling to her kitten

q.q: How did Mr Zhang help the kitten?
q.a: He climbed a ladder and took it down

q.q: How does Mr Zhang feel at the end?

5.text: On Saturday morning forty students from our school went to the beach, but not for a swim. We wore gloves and carried big plastic bags. The sand looked beautiful from far away, but when we came closer, we saw bottles, cans, bags and even an old shoe. Plastic is the biggest problem, because it does not rot. Sea birds and fish often eat small pieces of it by mistake, and many of them get sick. In three hours we filled sixty bags with rubbish! Our teacher took photos and put them on the school website. A local newspaper wrote a short story about us, too. At the end, we sorted the rubbish into groups for recycling. We were tired and dirty, but proud. From now on, we will bring our own water bottles and say no to plastic straws.

q.q: Why is plastic a big problem?
q.a: It does not rot and animals eat it

q.q: How many bags did the students fill?
What will the students do from now on?

5.text: Wilbur and Orville Wright were two brothers from America. They owned a small shop where they repaired and built bicycles, but their real dream was to fly. They studied birds carefully and noticed how their wings turned in the wind. In their workshop they built a wooden tunnel to test different wing shapes,. After many tests, they made a plane with an engine and two propellers. On a cold morning in December 1903, near a place called Kitty Hawk, Orville lay on the lower wing and flew for twelve seconds. It was a short flight, but it was the first time that a machine with a person on it had flown by its own power. Today millions of people fly every day.

q.q: What kind of shop did the brothers have?
How long was the first flight?
What is the main idea of the text?
q.a: Two brothers who kept trying made flying possible
w: Birds taught people to build bicycles
Kitty Hawk is a cold place

5.text: People celebrate in different ways in winter. In many Western countries, families celebrate Christmas on the twenty-fifth of December. They put up a tree in the living room, hang lights on it and give presents to each other. In Sweden, on the thirteenth of December, a girl wears a white dress and a crown with candles and brings sweet buns to her family. In India, people light small lamps for the festival of Diwali, which means a festival of light. In Japan, families eat noodles on the last evening of the year and listen to temple bells that ring one hundred and eight times. In China, we have the Spring Festival with dumplings and red envelopes. The customs are different, but the ideas are the same: families come together, share good food and hope for a happy new year.

q.q: What do people do in India for Diwali?
What do Japanese families do on the last evening?
q.a: Eat noodles and hear temple bells

q.q: What is the same in all the customs?
q.a: Families come together and share food

5.text: Long ago there lived a poor boy named Ma Liang. He loved to draw, but he had no money for a brush. One night an old man appeared in his dream and gave him a magic paintbrush. 'Everything you paint will become real,' he said. In the morning Ma Liang painted a bird, and it flew away singing. He painted a fish, and it swam in the river. He used his gift to help poor villagers, drawing ploughs for their fields and water for their dry land. A greedy king heard about the brush and ordered Ma Liang to come to his palace. 'Paint me a mountain of gold,' he said. Ma Liang refused, but the king locked him up. Later, the boy escaped by painting a door on the wall.
5.src: adapted from a Chinese folk tale (public domain)

q.q: What did Ma Liang get in his dream?
How did he help the villagers?
q.a: He drew ploughs and water for them

q.q: How did he escape from the king?
q.a: He painted a door on the wall

5.text: It is the last week of December, and Emma opens her diary. A year ago she wrote a list of wishes, and now she wants to see what happened. She wanted to improve her English, and she did: she read twelve short books and joined the school English club. She wanted to learn to swim, and in July she swam her first whole length of the pool. But she did not keep her promise to clean her room every week, and she smiles when she reads that line. Emma does not feel sad about it. Then she opens a new page and writes: 'Next year, I am going to visit my cousin in Canada, learn to cook three dishes and help at the animal shelter.' She closes the diary.

q.q: What did Emma do to improve her English?
q.a: She read books and joined the English club

q.q: Which wish did Emma not keep?
What is Emma going to do next year?
q.a: Visit her cousin and help at the animal shelter

6.text: On Saturday morning, Mei and her brother Tom went to the park with a red kite. The wind was strong, so the kite flew high above the trees. Suddenly the string broke! The kite danced across the sky and disappeared behind a tall building. Tom wanted to cry, but Mei said, “Don't worry. We will find it.” They walked along the river and asked an old man who was selling ice cream. “I saw a red kite near the school,” he said. The children hurried there. At last they saw it, caught on a branch of a small tree. A kind girl was standing under the tree. She had already tied the string to her bicycle. “Is this yours?” she asked with a smile. Tom took the kite and said thank you. That afternoon, the three children flew it together.

q.q: Why did the kite fly away?
w: Tom let it go on purpose

q.q: Where was the kite found?
What can we say about the girl under the tree?
w: She wanted to keep the kite
She was afraid of the children

6.text: One day a crow found a big piece of cheese. She flew to a high branch and sat down to enjoy her meal. A hungry fox walked under the tree. He smelled the cheese and wanted it very much, but he could not climb the tree. So he thought of a clever plan. “Good morning, Madam Crow,” he said. “How beautiful you look today! Your feathers shine like silk. I am sure your voice is also lovely. Would you sing one song for me?” The crow felt proud. She opened her beak to sing, “Caw, caw!” and the cheese fell to the ground. The fox caught it at once and ran away, laughing. The crow was sad and angry, but it was too late. From that day she never believed sweet words again.
6.src: adapted from Aesop's Fables, The Fox and the Crow (public domain)

q.q: Why could the fox not take the cheese himself?
q.a: He could not climb the tree

q.q: What is the main lesson of the story?
q.a: Do not trust people who only flatter you

q.q: In the text, the word “clever” is closest to

6.text: In many Chinese cities, night markets come alive after sunset. Last Friday, Lin went to one with her cousin Hao. The street was full of bright lights and delicious smells. Sellers called out loudly, “Fresh fruit! Hot noodles!” Lin wanted to try everything. First they bought grilled sweet potatoes, which were soft and warm. Then Hao found a small stall selling paper lanterns, and he chose a blue one for his mother. Lin watched an artist who made little animals from sugar. She was amazed at how fast his hands moved. At nine o'clock, the cousins were tired but happy. They shared a bowl of sweet soup and took the bus home. “Let's come again next month,” said Lin. Hao nodded. For both of them, the market was the best part of the week.

q.q: What did Hao buy for his mother?
What did Lin think of the sugar artist?
How did the cousins go home?

6.text: Look up on a sunny day and you will see a blue sky. But why is it blue? The answer is in the light from the sun. Sunlight looks white, but it is really made of many colours, like the colours of a rainbow. When this light enters the air around the Earth, it hits tiny pieces of gas. Blue light is scattered by these pieces much more than red light. This means blue light goes in every direction, so we see it from everywhere in the sky. At sunrise and sunset, the sunlight must travel through more air before it reaches our eyes. Most of the blue is scattered away, and we see red and orange instead. That is why the evening sky can be so beautiful. Next time you see a sunset, remember: it is science, not magic.

q.q: What is sunlight really made of?
Why do we see red at sunset?
q.a: The light travels through more air and the blue is scattered away
w: The air has no gas at that time

q.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
q.a: Science explains the colours of the sky

6.text: The Great Wall of China is one of the most famous buildings in the world. It is not one single wall. Instead, it is a long line of walls, towers and gates built by different rulers over more than two thousand years. The first emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang, joined several older walls together to protect his land from enemies in the north. Later, the Ming dynasty built the part that most tourists visit today, using strong bricks and stone. Soldiers lived in the towers and sent signals with smoke to warn others of danger. Many workers helped to build the wall, and the work was very hard. Today the Great Wall is not used for defence any more. Millions of visitors climb it every year, and people from all over the world enjoy its wonderful views and long history.

q.q: What is the Great Wall?
q.a: A long line of walls, towers and gates
w: A big city in the north

q.q: How did soldiers warn others of danger?
Who uses the Great Wall today?

6.text: Spring Festival is the most important holiday in China, and the dinner on New Year's Eve is the highlight. Xiao Yu's whole family gathers at her grandmother's house in a small village. The kitchen is busy all afternoon. Grandmother makes dumplings with her special filling, and everyone helps to wrap them. Xiao Yu's dumplings are not very pretty, but her grandmother always says, “They will taste perfect.” There is also a whole fish on the table, because the Chinese word for fish sounds like the word for extra, and people hope for more good things in the new year. After the meal, the adults give the children red envelopes with lucky money. Outside, fireworks light up the dark sky. Xiao Yu watches them from the window with a warm bowl of sweet rice balls. She feels thankful to be with her family.

q.q: Why is there a whole fish on the table?
q.a: The word for fish sounds like extra, a sign of good luck

q.q: What do the adults give the children?
How does Xiao Yu feel at the end?

6.text: Marie Curie was born in Poland in 1867. As a child she loved books and had an excellent memory. Her family was not rich, and in those days girls were not allowed to study at university in her country. So Marie saved money for years and went to Paris to continue her studies. She worked very hard, often with little food and a cold room. There she met Pierre Curie, a scientist, and they married. Together they studied a mysterious kind of energy and found two new elements. Marie named one of them polonium after her homeland. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and later she won a second one in a different science. Marie Curie showed the world that curiosity and hard work can open any door.

q.q: Why did Marie go to Paris?
q.a: To study, because girls could not go to university at home

q.q: Where does the name polonium come from?
What is special about Marie Curie's prizes?
q.a: She won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences
w: She won them with Pierre's help only
She won them as a child

6.text: Many people say that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. After a long night, your body needs fuel to start working. Children who skip breakfast often feel tired and find it hard to think in the morning lessons. A good breakfast has three parts. First, it needs some carbohydrates, such as bread, rice porridge or oats, which give you energy. Second, it should have protein, for example eggs, milk or beans, which help your muscles grow. Third, add some fruit or vegetables for vitamins. Try to avoid too much sugar. A sweet doughnut may taste great, but it gives you energy for only a short time, and then you feel hungry again. If you are always in a hurry, prepare something simple the night before, like a boiled egg and an apple. Your brain will thank you.

q.q: What does protein do for the body?
Why is a doughnut not a good breakfast?
q.a: It gives energy for only a short time
w: It is bad for the eyes

q.q: What is the advice for busy children?
q.a: Prepare something simple the night before

6.text: Every October, Green Hill School holds its sports day. This year, Ben was nervous. He was not a fast runner, but his class needed one more person for the relay race. “Please, Ben,” said his teacher. “We are a team.” On the big day, the sun was bright and the crowd was loud. Ben was the last runner in his team. When he took the stick, his class was in third place. His heart beat like a drum. He ran and ran, and slowly he passed the runner from Class Two. Then, only a few metres from the end, the runner from Class Five fell down. Ben stopped for one second and helped him up, and they finished together at the back. Everyone clapped louder than ever. Ben did not win, but his teacher said, “Today you won something better.”

q.q: Why did the class ask Ben to run?
q.a: They needed one more person for the relay

q.q: What did Ben do near the end?
What did the teacher mean by “something better”?
q.a: Kindness is worth more than a prize

6.text: When Mia arrived at school on Monday, she saw something strange in the classroom. A small white robot stood next to the teacher's desk. “This is Robo,” said Mr Chen. “He will help us learn science this term.” The children laughed and clapped. Robo could answer questions, show pictures on a screen and even tell jokes. “Why did the computer go to the doctor?” he asked. “Because it had a virus!” But he was not perfect. When Jack asked him about the colour of his own socks, Robo became confused, because robots do not wear socks. Mr Chen explained that a robot only knows what people teach it. “It is a tool, not a person,” he said. “It can help us think, but we must still decide for ourselves.” After a month, the whole class thought Robo was a good, funny friend.

q.q: What will Robo help the class with?
Why was Robo confused about socks?
What is Mr Chen's main message?
q.a: A robot is a tool, and people must still decide
w: Robots should be afraid of viruses

6.text: Every year, sea turtles swim thousands of kilometres to lay their eggs on the beach where they were born. At night, the mother turtle digs a hole in the sand, lays about a hundred eggs and goes back to the sea. Two months later, the baby turtles come out and rush towards the water. But today these animals face many dangers. Plastic bags in the ocean look like jellyfish, and turtles eat them by mistake. Bright city lights confuse the babies, so they walk the wrong way. Some people also take the eggs. Luckily, many volunteers now help. They protect the nests with small fences, switch off lights near the beach and clean the sand. You can help too. Use fewer plastic bags, join a beach clean-up and tell your friends. Small actions together can save a very old animal.

q.q: Why do turtles eat plastic bags?
How do city lights hurt baby turtles?
q.a: The babies walk the wrong way
w: The lights hurt their eyes only

q.q: What can ordinary people do?
q.a: Use fewer plastic bags and join clean-ups

6.text: A hare once laughed at a tortoise because he walked so slowly. “You are the slowest animal in the forest,” said the hare. The tortoise answered calmly, “Let us have a race, and we will see.” The hare thought it was a great joke, but he agreed. The other animals gathered to watch. At the signal, the hare shot forward like an arrow and soon left the tortoise far behind. Halfway along the path he stopped. “I have plenty of time,” he said, and lay down under a tree for a nap. Meanwhile, the tortoise kept walking, slowly but without stopping. Step by step, he passed the sleeping hare. When the hare finally woke up and ran to the end, he saw the tortoise already there, and all the animals were cheering. Slow and steady wins the race.
6.src: adapted from Aesop's Fables, The Hare and the Tortoise (public domain)

q.q: Why did the hare stop halfway?
q.a: He felt sure he would win and wanted to sleep
w: The tortoise asked him to stop

q.q: What did the tortoise do?
w: He slept under a tree too

q.q: What is the lesson?
q.a: Steady effort beats pride and speed

6.text: Omar and his father were driving across the desert when the car suddenly stopped. The engine made a strange noise and then went silent. There was no phone signal, and the nearest town was fifty kilometres away. “Stay calm,” said his father. “Panic is our worst enemy.” They remembered their guide's advice: never leave the car, because a car is easier to see than a person. They put a bright blue cloth on the roof and stayed in the shade. They drank water slowly and kept a small supply for later. When the night came, the desert became cold, so they wore all their jackets. At sunrise, Omar heard a distant sound. A truck was coming along the road! His father waved the cloth in the air, and the driver stopped. “You were lucky,” said the driver. “But you were also clever.”

q.q: Why did they stay with the car?
q.a: A car is easier to see than a person
w: The desert was safe at night

q.q: What did they put on the roof?
What does the driver mean by “clever”?

6.text:
Sam: Excuse me, I'd like to borrow some books about space. Can you help me?
Librarian: Of course. We have a good section on astronomy. It's on the second floor, near the window.
Sam: Thank you. How many books can I borrow at one time?
Librarian: Students can take four books for three weeks. If you need more time, you can renew them online.
Sam: What if I lose a book?
Librarian: Then you will have to pay for it, so please take care of them. Do you have a library card?
Sam: Not yet. I'm new in this town.
Librarian: No problem. Fill in this form and show me your school card. It only takes five minutes.
Sam: Great! Is it quiet upstairs?
Librarian: Yes, and there are comfortable chairs. Remember to keep your voice low, because many people are reading and studying.
Sam: I will. Thanks for your help!

q.q: How many books can a student borrow?
What does Sam need to get a library card?
q.a: Fill in a form and show his school card

q.q: What can we infer about Sam?
q.a: He has just moved to the town

6.text: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers, and their wings work like flippers in the water. Emperor penguins, the biggest kind, live in Antarctica, the coldest place on Earth. In winter, the temperature can fall below minus forty degrees, and strong winds blow across the ice. To stay warm, thousands of penguins stand close together in a huge group. Those on the outside slowly move to the middle, and others take their place, so everyone gets a turn to be warm. After the mother lays one egg, she goes to the sea to find food. The father keeps the egg on his feet, under a warm fold of skin, for about two months without eating. When the mother returns, the chick is born, and now it is her turn to care for it. Penguin families really work as a team.

q.q: How do penguins stay warm in winter?
q.a: They stand close together and take turns in the middle
w: They fly to a warmer place
They dig holes in the ground

q.q: Who keeps the egg warm first?
What is the main idea?
q.a: Penguins survive the cold by working together

6.text: The Mid-Autumn Festival is on the fifteenth day of the eighth month in the lunar calendar. On that night, the moon is round and very bright, and Chinese families get together to enjoy it. A round moon is a symbol of a whole and happy family. People eat mooncakes, which are small round cakes with sweet or salty fillings. Many children carry colourful lanterns and walk in the park. There is also a famous legend about the festival. Long ago, a woman named Chang'e drank a magic potion and floated up to the moon. They say she still lives there with a white rabbit, who makes medicine. Her husband, Hou Yi, put out her favourite food every year to remember her. Even today, when people are far from home, they look at the same moon and think of their families.

q.q: What does a round moon mean to Chinese families?
Who lives on the moon in the legend?
Why do people far from home look at the moon?
w: They want to go to the moon
They are afraid of the dark

6.text: Alexander Graham Bell was born in Scotland in 1847. His mother was almost deaf, and his father taught people how to speak clearly. Because of this, young Alexander became interested in sound. As an adult, he moved to America and worked as a teacher of deaf students. In his free time, he tried to find a way to send the human voice along a wire. This was not easy, and he made many mistakes. In 1876, in his small workshop in Boston, he spilled some acid by accident and called to his helper, “Mr Watson, come here, I want to see you.” Watson heard the words through the machine in another room. It was the first successful telephone call. Within a few years, telephones appeared in homes and offices across the country, and the way people talk to each other changed forever.

q.q: Why was Bell interested in sound?
q.a: His mother was almost deaf and his father taught speech
w: He wanted to be a doctor

q.q: What happened in 1876?
q.a: The first successful telephone call was made

q.q: What did telephones change?
q.a: How people talk to each other

6.text: On Tuesday, our regular teacher was ill, and a substitute teacher came to class. He was a tall man with a very serious face. “Good morning,” he said. “My name is Mr Brown. I do not like noise, and I do not like jokes.” The class became silent. Then he began to write on the board, but all the chalk broke, one piece after another. Mr Brown looked at the chalk, then at us. A small boy at the back whispered, “Maybe the chalk does not like your face.” Everyone tried not to laugh, but Mr Brown suddenly smiled. “That is the best joke I heard this year,” he said. “Perhaps I like jokes a little.” After that, the lesson was the funniest of the term. On Wednesday, we asked our teacher if Mr Brown could come again. She said she was a little jealous.

q.q: Why did a substitute teacher come?
What did the boy at the back say?
q.a: The chalk might not like Mr Brown's face

q.q: How did Mr Brown change during the lesson?
q.a: He became friendly and enjoyed the joke

6.text: A bee does not make honey for humans. It makes honey as food for the whole hive, especially for winter. The work begins when a worker bee flies from flower to flower. She sucks a sweet liquid called nectar and stores it in a special stomach. Back at the hive, she passes the nectar to another bee, and this bee passes it on to others. During this journey, natural substances in the bees' bodies change the nectar. Then the bees put it into small wax cells and fan it with their wings. The water slowly dries out, and the thick, sweet honey remains. Finally, they cover the cell with a layer of wax to keep it fresh. To make just one small spoon of honey, a single bee must work for her whole life. Next time you eat honey, remember how much work is in it.

q.q: Why do bees make honey?
q.a: As food for the hive, especially in winter

q.q: How does the nectar become thick honey?
q.a: The bees fan it so the water dries out
w: They cook it in the sun
They put it in the fridge

q.q: What is the main idea of the last sentence?
q.a: Honey is the result of a lot of work

6.text: On a warm farm, a mother duck sat on her eggs. One by one the eggs broke, and the little yellow ducklings came out. But the last egg was bigger, and the bird inside was grey and clumsy. The other animals laughed at him. “You are so ugly,” they said, and even his brothers pushed him away. The sad duckling ran away from the farm. He lived alone by a lake through the cold winter, and he was often hungry. At last spring came. One morning, he saw some beautiful white birds on the water. He wanted to join them, but he expected them to laugh at him as well. He bent his head down, and then he saw his reflection in the water. He was not a duckling at all. He was a lovely swan! The other swans welcomed him, and he was never lonely again.
6.src: adapted from Hans Christian Andersen, The Ugly Duckling (public domain)

q.q: Why did the duckling leave the farm?
q.a: The others laughed at him and pushed him away
w: He wanted to learn to swim

q.q: What did he see in the water?
What is the main message?
q.a: Do not judge others by how they look when they are young

6.text: The Amazon is the biggest rainforest in the world. It covers parts of nine countries in South America, and most of it is in Brazil. Through the forest flows the Amazon River, which carries more water than any other river on Earth. The climate here is hot and wet all year, so plants grow very fast. About one in ten of all known animal species lives in this forest, from tiny frogs to jaguars and giant snakes. Millions of insects also live there, and many of them have not even been named. The trees produce a lot of oxygen and take in carbon dioxide, so people sometimes call the rainforest the lungs of the Earth. Sadly, every year large areas are cut down for farms and roads. Scientists and local people are working together to protect what remains, because the loss of this forest would affect the whole planet.

q.q: In which country is most of the Amazon?
Why is the rainforest called the lungs of the Earth?
q.a: The trees produce oxygen and take in carbon dioxide
w: It is a very quiet place

q.q: Why are large areas being cut down?

6.text: Captain Lee had a grey cat called Sailor. The cat lived on the old fishing boat and loved the sea more than the land. Every morning, Sailor sat at the front of the boat and watched the waves. One day, when the boat was far from the harbour, a storm came quickly. Dark clouds covered the sky, and big waves hit the boat. The captain tried to turn back, but the wind was too strong. Suddenly, Sailor jumped onto the captain's shoulder and made a loud noise, looking to the left. Captain Lee looked and saw a small, quiet bay between the rocks. He steered the boat there, and soon the water was calm. They waited until the storm was over. After that, the fishermen in the village said that Sailor was the cleverest cat in the world, and they always gave him the best fish.

q.q: What did Sailor do during the storm?
q.a: He showed the captain a safe bay

q.q: Why could the captain not simply turn back?
w: He did not know the way

q.q: How did the villagers feel about Sailor afterwards?
q.a: They thought he was very clever

6.text: It was raining heavily, so Anna and her friend Leo had to stay in the old house of Anna's grandfather. They were bored until Leo noticed something strange in the attic: a small wooden box under a pile of old coats. It had no key, but on the lid there were four letters, each one on a little wheel. “It needs a code,” said Leo. They tried their names, but nothing happened. Then Anna remembered a photo downstairs. It showed her grandfather as a boy, and on the back someone had written a year: 1958. She turned the wheels to the numbers, and the box opened with a click. Inside lay an old compass and a note. It said, “For the person who is brave enough to go and find the next adventure.” The children looked at each other and smiled.

q.q: Where did they find the box?
q.a: In the attic under old coats
w: Behind a door in the kitchen

q.q: How did Anna find the code?
q.a: A year was written on the back of an old photo

q.q: What was inside the box?

6.text: Why do we need sleep? Scientists have found that sleep is not just a rest for the body. While you sleep, your brain is very busy. It sorts the things you learned during the day and moves important memories to a safe place. That is why students who sleep well often do better in tests. Sleep also helps your body to grow and to fight illness. Children between six and twelve years old need about nine to eleven hours every night. If they sleep much less, they may feel angry, forget things easily or have trouble paying attention. To sleep well, follow some simple rules. Go to bed at the same time every night. Turn off screens at least one hour before, because their bright light tells the brain it is still daytime. Keep your room dark and quiet. Tonight, try going to bed a little earlier.

q.q: What does the brain do during sleep?
q.a: It sorts what you learned and saves memories

q.q: Why should you turn off screens before bed?
q.a: Their bright light tells the brain it is still daytime

q.q: How much sleep do children aged six to twelve need?

6.text: More than two thousand years ago, a network of trade routes joined China with Central Asia and Europe. Later people called it the Silk Road, because Chinese silk was one of the most valuable goods that travelled along it. Merchants did not usually go the whole way. Instead, they carried their goods to a town on the road, sold them, and other traders took them further. The journey crossed hot deserts and high mountains, so camels, which can walk for days without water, were very important. Besides silk, tea and paper went west, while grapes, spices and glass came east. But the road carried more than goods. Ideas, religions, music and stories also travelled along it. The famous traveller Zhang Qian was sent by the Han emperor to find friends in the west, and his journeys opened the way for this great exchange between cultures.

q.q: Why were camels important?
q.a: They can walk for days without water
w: They carried silk to Europe alone

q.q: What went from west to east along the road?
Besides goods, what else travelled on the Silk Road?
